item.title: Bears vs. Packers live updates, inactives, where to watch: Tyson Bagent starts for Caleb Williams, Green Bay seeks first home win of the season at Lambeau
item.description: The Packers are still seeking their first win at Lambeau this season.
item.content:encoded:
We've got ourselves an NFC North showdown in Week 5, as the Chicago Bears travel to Lambeau to face the Green Bay Packers in their first of two matchups this season. The Bears lead the division with a 3-1 record, while the Packers sit at 2-2 despite a fairly ugly start to the season.

Chicago is once again without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who is yet to practice since going down with a hamstring injury in Week 2. That means it will be Tyson Bagent again at quarterback, who will look to build on last week's win over the Jets after another week's worth of reps, where Bagent threw for 268 yards and a pick. Expect them to continue to lean on the run game on the back of a monster outing from Kyle Monangai, who talled 146 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Week 4.

The Packers are still seeking their first win at Lambeau this season after getting upset by the Atlanta Falcons in their home opener in Week 3, cranking up the heat on head coach Matt LaFleur after a relatively slow start. Even their two wins this season (at Jets, at Buccaneers) were closer than they should have been, outscoring both teams — who hold a combined record of 1-7 — by just a field goal.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Chicago Bears face the Green Bay Packers in Week 5, airing on Fox.

item.description: Follow along with all of Sunday's action in Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
We've got another action-packed NFL game slate for Week 5, albeit a slate short of two teams — the Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers, which are both on bye. Per usual, fantasy football managers and NFL fans have a number of injuries to monitor ahead of kickoff.

Among those questionable for Week 5: Bengals WRs Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor/neck), Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (foot), Vikings WR Justin Jefferson (ankle), Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle).

There were a number of stars ruled out ahead of Sunday's action, including Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (with Tyler Huntley getting the start), Eagles RB Saquon Barkley and WR DeVonta Smith, Jets RB Breece Hall and Bears RB Kyle Monangai. On the defensive side of the ball, two teams will be without their star cornerbacks, with Christian Gonzalez ruled out for the Patriots and Pat Surtain II out for the Broncos.

The Cardinals will notably be without WR Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday, reportedly informing him that he'd sit out for Week 5 while they attempt to finalize a trade, moving on from the former No. 4 overall pick. It has been reported that the Texans are one team involved in potential trade talks.

One player who didn't carry an injury designation for Week 5 is Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, who is making his return from a dislocated elbow in his non-throwing arm this afternoon against the New York Giants. He missed just two games, which did not require surgery, though he will wear a brace on that elbow to prevent any further injury to the elbow. He'll be short on receiving options in this contest, as wide receiver Stefon Diggs has been ruled out, while Terry McLaurin is questionable with a hamstring injury that held him out of Week 4.

item.title: Eagles vs. Jaguars score, live updates: Trevor Lawrence makes eighth London start with Jags on a hot streak
item.description: The Jaguars are 16-5 over their last 21 regular-season games.
item.content:encoded:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are back in London for Week 5, playing host as the home team against the Philadelphia Eagles. Kickoff is set for 9:30 a.m. ET at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, airing live on NFL Network.

The Eagles got off to a 2-2 start and have generally underwhelmed this season, with their usually strong run game off to a disappointing start. Saquon Barkley is out in Week 5 after suffering a hamstring injury last week, with his backup Tank Bigsby also out after being placed on IR this week after core muscle surgery. They're also down their top receiving weapon, as DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is set to miss his second consecutive game. The team also traded away OL Cam Jergens this week, while All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement this week.

Simply put … Philadelphia has a lot going on heading into this matchup.

The Jaguars continue to look hot under head coach Liam Coen, and playing in what's essentially a home game across the pond, sportsbooks are thinking that momentum will continue with Jacksonville favored by more than a touchdown. It's not just the offense, either, which is clicking for sixth-year quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Their defense has looked good too, forcing a turnover on a league-high 21.6% of drives faced, while allowing a score on just 29.7% of drives faced — the third-lowest rate in the league.

item.title: Jalyx Hunt injury: Eagles edge rusher leaves game in pain
item.description: The Eagles defense takes another hit to an already thin depth chart.
item.content:encoded:
Things went from bad to worse for the Eagles defense. Just after they were able to make an impressive stop to keep the Jaguars from tying the game before halftime, Jalyx Hunt suffered an injury to his lower left leg, with the edge rusher clutching his ankle area as he took a hit while his leg was locked underneath.

Hunt refusing the cart to the locker room is encouraging, but he was clearly in a lot of pain as he was helped inside. Seems unlikely he returns on Sunday, but hopefully it’s not something that will keep him out long term. Aside from Hunts physicality and skill, he also always brings the energy and is an important piece of what the defense does.

For many reasons this is not great, but the lack of depth is astounding. Jonathan Greenard being inactive was a game-time decision, and the team also lost LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who was ejected in the early seconds of the game.

With Hunt out, the Eagles have three healthy edge rushers remaining: Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa.

item.title: NFL today: How to watch 49ers v Seahawks, TV channels & live stream Sunday 11 October
item.description: How will the Seahawks and 49ers fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options
item.content:encoded:
Last winter, two games between the 49ers and Seahawks decided the shape of the NFL season. The two teams played each other in the Bay Area on the last weekend of the regular season, and Seattle’s win secured the NFC West and homefield advantage when the teams met later in the NFC divisional playoffs. Seattle’s advantage only got more lopsided at home, and a 41-6 win proved to be the launching pad that sent the Seahawks flying through the rest of the playoffs, ending with a Super Bowl victory. The Niners watched from home.

Now they meet again in one of the most anticipated games of the 2026 season to date. The 49ers take an unbeaten record on the road against a 3-1 Seattle team who have kept the train on the tracks despite Sam Darnold getting hurt early in Week 1 and missing a game. Whoever wins here will claim divisional favorite status as we move into the second quarter of the season, and they’ll also give themselves a good shot to claim a head-to-head tiebreaker that may be important in the league’s most competitive division.

49ers at Seahawks

Time:4.25pm ET/9:25pm BST

Stadium:Lumen Field (Seattle, Washington)

How to watch

United States: Watch on Fox or stream on Fox One or Fubo (where the local Fox affiliate carries the game).

Canada: Stream on DAZN and Fubo

United Kingdom: Watch on Sky Sports NFL or stream on NOW

What to watch for

The main man to watch for Seattle is the same as ever: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who just had one of the handful of most productive receiving seasons ever and is so far averaging more yards per game (120) than he did when he won Offensive Player of the Year. The Seahawks do not have a clear No 2 wideout and have some running back problems, too, given that Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker now plays for the Chiefs and first-round rookie Jadarian Price went to injured reserve this week. But as long as an offense has JSN, it has a chance to put up serious point totals. The Seahawks’ 105 points in four games are tied for sixth in the NFC. They’ll rise up the ranks if non-JSN contributors emerge.

The 49ers are a more balanced juggernaut at the moment. Brock Purdy continues to be Brock Purdy, putting up terrific numbers in a maximally supportive system. A large handful of offensive players on the wrong side of 30 have all maintained their access to the fountain of youth: Trent Williams blocking, Christian McCaffrey running and catching, and Mike Evans, George Kittle, and Deebo Samuel as downfield targets. An injured defensive front (currently missing star edge rusher Nick Bosa and tackle James Thompson) has not stopped the 49ers’ defense from giving up the third-fewest yards per play in the NFL. The only trouble is that the two teams ahead of them are the Seahawks and Rams. Will this division put three teams in the playoff again? It looks that way.

item.title: After playing in London, Colts have an added disadvantage on Sunday at Steelers
item.description: The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams.

The Week 4 and Week 5 games in 2026 include a glitch about which the Colts should not be thrilled.

They got the shoulder tap to fly to London for a game against the Commanders last Sunday. This week, after returning from England, the Colts travel to Pittsburgh for a game against the Steelers.

Meanwhile, the Steelers had a bus trip to and from Cleveland for a Week 4 Thursday night game, followed by a mini-bye while their next foe was playing overseas.

It's a basic issue of competitive integrity that will take a back seat to the ongoing obsession with global expansion. And the league will gloss over such irregularities because there's nothing that can be done to eliminate the annoyances and inconveniences that come from expecting teams to make long trips for games on foreign soil and to return home for the next game on the slate.

That's one of the reasons why the league hopes to get clearance from the NFL Players Association to stage 16 international games per year. If every team has to travel to and from another country once per season, the hassle is largely balanced out.

Still, there's something to be said for also ensuring that any team that plays on a given Sunday in another country will be facing on the following Sunday a team that played on Sunday or Monday, and not on the preceding Thursday. That part was avoidable for the 2026 schedule — and it was not avoided.

Boston surpassed this number three times in the first four weeks. That includes a four-catch, 89-yard showing against Pittsburgh Thursday night. Even in the game he missed the mark, he still had 41 yards. The Jets gave up 250 yards to Detroit and 260 to Chicago through the air the last two weeks.

Wilson faces a Detroit defense that just made Tetairoa McMillan look like prime Jerry Rice. He caught 18 balls the last two weeks and should easily clear six here.

Tate is the Titans’ #1 receiving option. He beat this number each of the last two weeks, especially because the Titans play from behind a lot.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 5
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks shares the Blueprint to the WR position for Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column, this WR column on Thursdays and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Puka Nacua (vs. BUF) - 92.5 proj. receiving yards

Nacua's "pre-hernia" injury could be a serious long-term issue, but while he's in the lineup, he has the best projection every week. He got the best of an impressive Eagles secondary last week (WR5 on WR7 usage) while re-entering the lineup, and this matchup is far easier. The Rams have a monster 28.75-point team total (third) while hosting the Bills on Monday Night Football. Buffalo has allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs this year, including a 2-TD game from Romeo Doubs (WR8) on top of big games from Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9). They've missed CB1 Christian Benford recently, and the size issue from CB2 Maxwell Hairston will be one the Rams will certainly target here. They've allowed five TDs on just 27 man coverage reps this year.

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (vs. SF) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN drafters on Yahoo have won 62% of their games, the highest of any WR through four weeks. He's the WR1 overall on WR3 overall usage, averaging a ridiculous 120 YPG on 10.3 targets.

Smith-Njigba faced the 49ers five times since 2024, scoring 7.8, 9.4, 11.4, 14.9, and 16.8 half PPR points in them. He's only scored a touchdown once in them while clearing 84 yards in 3 of 5. They've played him well all things considered, but their lack of pass rush right now works in JSN's favor. The Seahawks are at home with a 24.25-point team total (ninth). The 49ers gave up a score to Jaylen Waddle last week and Michael Wilson finished as the WR4 overall the week prior. It's a totally fine matchup for JSN.

3. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at ARI) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

St. Brown is the WR5 on WR1 overall usage this season. His 11.5 targets per game keep him on pace for 196 targets this year. Dating back to last year, St. Brown has cleared 14.2 expected half PPR points in eight straight games with the Lions' secondary falling apart.

The Lions project for a league-high 30.0 points this week against a sorry Cardinals defense. They've allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including top-17 finishes to Malik Nabers (WR10), Deebo Samuel (WR17), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR1) and Ladd McConkey (WR11). It's go time.

4. CeeDee Lamb (vs. TB) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb has 25 receiving first downs this year, only trailing 2011 Wes Welker for the most in NFL history through four weeks. He's shredded the Ravens and Texans defenses most recently, too. Lamb played a season-high 38% snaps in the slot to get away from CB1 Derek Stingley, including on his game-winning in-cut versus safety Jalen Pitre. It's a well-coached offense with quality protection and elite skill players. Dallas will compete for the scoring title. Lamb is the WR2 on WR4 usage so far, leading in receptions (9.3 per game) and yards (125 per game).

The blitz-heavy Bucs can catch bad OLs and QBs by surprise, but Prescott is amongst the best against the blitz over years of data. Lamb can be a quick outlet, as he was last week, but he can also get downfield where the Bucs have been exposed by Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) recently. Dallas has a 29.0-point team total (second).

5. Ja'Marr Chase (at MIA)

6. Michael Wilson (vs. DET) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Michael Wilson was so good that Marvin Harrison Jr. is being traded. He won't play here.

Wilson has some of the best WR tape of 2026. He's a great route runner at the top of his break, he's physical and he has moments at the catch point. His third-and-1 deep out route last week was sensational stuff. Down six points with seconds remaining at the 5-yard line, Wilson was targeted on first-, second- and fourth-down. Were they completed? No, but that's a great sign that he's trusted down there.

Through four weeks, Wilson is the WR22 on WR6 usage. Since Week 11 of last year, Wilson only trails Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave and Amon-Ra St. Brown in fantasy points per game (15.5). He's WR2 in air yards per game and WR3 in targets per game during that stretch, too. I think he's far more of a fantasy WR2 than the market believes.

The matchup is the best one in the NFL. WR rooms facing the Lions are averaging 56 more yards per game against them compared to the rest of their schedule right now, easily the most in the NFL. They desperately miss S Brian Branch (Achilles) and other starting CBs, and they're put in tough spots because the Lions offense is scoring at will. Just look at Tetairoa McMillan (WR1 overall), Garrett Wilson (WR3) and Chris Olave (WR6 without a TD) versus the Lions. The Cardinals project for 24.5 points at home, while the Lions have a league-leading 30.0 total. Get excited.

7. Drake London (vs. BAL) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

In 14 games with Michael Penix Jr. since 2024, London is now the WR3 (17.2 half PPR points) on WR8 usage (15.8 expected), WR1 overall target share (35%) and WR1 overall air yards (116 per game). He's finished as the WR2 overall and the WR24 overall (without a TD) in his two games with him this year. Penix has executed his under-center play action reps and is moving just enough to have a productive season. Penix wants to drive the ball, and London is running more deep breaking routes in this offense to fit in. There will be some underneath work, but London could be a killer on intermediate throws. Penix had an awesome anticipation throw before a zone defender had time to make a play on the ball on a corner route last night. London has an obvious case to be an early Round 2 pick if drafting today.

The Ravens have a good defense, but they are still working out the kinks and don't have an overpowering pass-rushing unit in general. They've allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including a career-high 145 yards to Carnell Tate last week. CeeDee Lamb (WR13) and Chris Olave (WR9) had their usual games against them as clear-cut top targets. Atlanta has a 23.25-point team total (12th) at home.

8. Nico Collins (at TEN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins is the WR3 on WR5 usage this season, averaging 9.0 targets per game as one of the most dominant players on tape. There is no competition for targets in Houston with its run game in shambles once again; it'd make sense to start leaning into the pass game more than ever. CJ Stroud is playing well.

The matchup is also a solid one. Houston has a 23.0-point team total (13th) in Tennessee, and its defense is far more dominant at DT than anywhere else right now. Teams should be comfortable passing against them in neutral situations. I've seen DeVonta Smith (WR6), Dontayvion Wicks (WR27) and Zay Flowers (WR6) give them major trouble this year. CB1 Alontae Taylor and CB2 Cor'Dale Flott are players to target as mismatches for Collins' size and speed. He has 79+ yards or a TD in all five career games against the Titans, including a WR4 overall finish in Week 11 last season.

9. Davante Adams (vs. BUF) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Adams is the WR16 on WR6 usage in 18 games with Puka Nacua since last year. He busted last week after multiple fingertip missed plays for explosives and touchdowns, but the underlying numbers were otherwise there with WR10 expected points (15.6) and nine targets. Nacua is a baller still but also maybe a step slower while playing with this "pre-hernia" injury, and Adams is moving quite well on tape right now.

The matchup with the Bills is tasty. It's at home with extra rest on Monday Night Football, and they've been shredded by physical WRs this year, especially without CB1 Christian Benford. Romeo Doubs (WR8) and Efton Chism III had SportsCenter moments last week, while Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9) did their thing in previous outings. A 28.75-point team total (third) is the final obvious tell to start Adams as an upside WR1/2.

10. Justin Jefferson (at NO)

Jefferson (ankle) expects to play after missing last week with a low-ankle sprain, even with the Vikings having a bye next week. They'd only let him play if he was truly ready to go given that context. I'm not docking him for injury. Jordan Addison is also dealing with a hamstring injury, though he was back at practice Thursday.

11. Chris Olave (vs. MIN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has a seven-game streak of 15+ half PPR points and 14+ expected half PPR points. He's the WR6 overall on WR2 usage this year with Tyler Shough comfortably leading the NFL in dropbacks. He'd be an early Round 2 pick if redrafting today.

The Vikings will easily be the toughest test yet, especially with LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (IR) being replaced by an inexperienced player who is allowing a near league-high rate of pressures. That gets turned up against DC Brian Flores, who is as good as anyone in league history at destroying protection rules. They also play with two deep safeties often, so it's a bit harder to find the explosive plays that have made Olave one of the best fantasy WRs in the game. Minnesota has allowed the 19th-most fantasy points to WRs, largely driven by a massive downfield outing from Christian Watson (WR2) in Week 1. They haven't allowed a top-30 fantasy WR since then versus the Dolphins, Bucs and Bears. The Saints project for 19.5 points (22nd), far fewer than normal.

12. George Pickens (vs. TB) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens is the most obvious buy-low ever. He's only the WR39 on WR23 usage this season, but the tape is showing plenty of DPIs called on him and some bad luck. There will be huge games coming with the Cowboys already leading the NFL in points per drive (3.4) without star LG Tyler Smith, who returns for Thursday Night Football. Dating back to last year, Pickens is the WR17 on WR12 usage with 22% of the targets in games with CeeDee Lamb.

The Cowboys are projected for the second-most points at home against an 0-4 Bucs team. This historically is a pass-funnel defense, and the Todd Bowles blitzes aren't going to catch Dak Prescott by surprise as much as they've worked against lesser offenses. Splash plays from Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) are reasons for upside WR2 faith. We can panic if Pickens doesn't come through tonight ...

13. Christian Watson (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson had his worst game of the year last week, but nothing has materially changed other than Tucker Kraft is becoming more involved after a horrible start to his season coming off a torn ACL. That could hurt Watson at the margins, especially when (if) Josh Jacobs returns. Watson is still the WR8 on WR12 usage and WR14 targets per game (7.8).

A matchup with the Bears may be a little more difficult than it seemed pre-season after DC Dennis Allen has gotten the most of his injured defense, but it's still a fun game to target. Jalen Coker had a WR1 overall finish against them in Week 1, for crying out loud. The Packers are projected for 22.0 points (16th) as slight home dogs. Watson had three games against the Bears last year; 36 yards with a score in the playoff loss, a 17-yard dud in Week 16 and a WR5 overall finish in Week 14.

14. Zay Flowers (at ATL) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Flowers is not expected to have Lamar Jackson this time around, which obviously impacts his efficiency a ton, but OC Declan Doyle is very reliant on Flowers being the focal point of the pass game. He's being used underneath in ways that should keep his floor high with Tyler Huntley at QB. His yards per route being in his own stratosphere is helpful when readjusting for his new situation. He's the WR6 on WR15 usage, including two half-games.

The matchup is a strong one, too. The Falcons are well coached but down CB1 A.J. Terrell and two impact pass rushers. They've allowed the fourth-most passing yards per game (277) and seventh-most fantasy points to WRs so far. Chris Olave (116 yards), Christian Watson (96 yards) and Tetairoa McMillan (101 yards) all have been excellent as the top targets in their offenses against them recently. Baltimore's 20.25-point team total is just about seven points less than normal, and Derrick Henry's has a disproportionate touchdown share in this offense.

15. Matthew Golden (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden is the WR17 on WR10 usage and WR9 targets per game (9.0) this season, with 10+ half PPR points and 10+ expected half PPR points in 3-of-4 contests. He's been a more explosive version of the Romeo Doubs role from last year, but now there's not a No. 3 receiver to get "gimme" looks. Those can trickle down to Golden, too.

See more about the matchup in the Christian Watson blurb from above, noting the primary difference is Golden's matchup with CB2 Tyrique Stevenson is far better than against CB1 Jaylon Johnson.

16. Jaylen Waddle (at LAC) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Waddle's season-long ceiling isn't hitting as we'd hoped. His 21% target share and WR37 expected half PPR points sit too far down to be trusted as more than an inconsistent WR2/3 in fantasy. Bo Nix's quick trigger to the checkdown has left some potential intermediate and downfield throws on the field, and the Sean Payton offense will always have schemed up targets to others. Waddle did have two screen receptions in Week 4, and his overall involvement could tick up with valued WR3 Pat Bryant (IR, ankle) now injured. Waddle has also dropped a couple of passes for potential explosives this year to tilt us further. He's the WR32 per game. I'm waiting for the 50-yard YAC moment ...

17. Garrett Wilson (vs. CLE) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson was rug-pulled by a Jets outing that resulted in the fourth-fewest plays (32) in a single game in NFL history. The Bears also did a good job of limiting Wilson on their dropbacks, but that will go down as an outlier game. Wilson was the WR15 on WR25 usage and the WR3 on WR9 usage in the previous two outings with Breece Hall (quad), AD Mitchell (finger) and Mason Taylor (thumb) all sidelined. They're all still injured, so Wilson's ceiling is far higher than usual.

The Browns are the only team in the NFL actually playing man coverage at a notable rate. They've used it 88 times. The next closest is at 57, by the Patriots. They can do it because CB1 Denzel Ward is having another great season, and they are enjoying a great season from S Ronnie Hickman. This will be a "ball up top" matchup. The Jets are projected for 21.0 points (21st) while at home.

18. Parker Washington (vs. PHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

19. Jameson Williams (at ARI) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Dud-dud-dud-boom. That's the story with Jamo. He had three comeback receptions, one screen, one quick out and one go ball Cover 3 hole shot heading into halftime in a wild loss to the Panthers. His day could've been bigger had he come down with two designed chunk plays (double move down the sideline and bootleg play-action dig). Williams ultimately finished WR19 on WR20 usage without scoring a touchdown, and the fact that the Lions defense yet again couldn't get stops bodes well for Williams' WR3 odds this year. He's been the WR45 on WR33 usage this season as a positive regression candidate.

20. DK Metcalf (vs. IND) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

21. Tee Higgins (at MIA)

Update: He was a full participant on Friday. Let's roll???

22. Malik Nabers (at WAS) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: The conditions are quite rainy, and Nabers has seemed sensitive to his knee this week.

Hand up — I got this one way wrong last week when I ranked him closer to the WR3 range. Nabers was the WR10 on WR30 usage with multiple explosives. He beat a heavy-footed LB on a seam ball for a TD, high-pointed a lollipop from Jameis Winston on a deep corner route and had a great circus route with massive separation. There was some underneath success, too, including a hitch route that led to two broken tackles. We're inching closer to 90% health as we head into October, and with the Giants at 3-1, it'll likely be Jameis for the near future. Nabers is trending upwards as the WR33 on WR38 usage this season.

The matchup is a great one. The Commanders are doing the chaos at the line of scrimmage thing a lot more than others with new DC Daronte Jones (from the Brian Flores tree), and it's funneled a lot more yards via the air (eighth-most) than on the ground (27th). Star WRs have had big outings against them already; JSN (WR1 overall) and CeeDee Lamb (WR3 overall). There's no reason to believe in Mike Sainristill in boundary coverage right now. The Giants project for 19.0 points (26th), however and it will almost always be a fairly run-heavy plan under Harbaugh.

23. Tre' Harris (vs. DEN)

Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston are both out. Harris and Orande Gadsden are the only pass-catchers with substantial playing time experience with Justin Herbert. The Chargers have combined for 20.9 expected half PPR points as a team this year, and Harris should absorb about half of it this week. The Broncos won't have their top-2 boundary CBs this week and haven't been quite as good as normal this year with changes across their DL as well.

24. Mike Evans (at SEA) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

25. Romeo Doubs (vs. LV) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Doubs has been the wildest rollercoaster of the year, but Week 4 was nothing but a total smash. Aside from an extremely low ball that was tossed by Doubs into the air for an INT, Doubs played well. He had a skinny post TD, a 4th-and-3 slant win and a one-handed fade TD. His WR8 finish was on WR11 expected half PPR points, and the Patriots also lost Mack Hollins (calf) around halftime. They're running out of bodies for Drake Maye to throw to, so Doubs' value is absolutely trending up. His expected half PPR points have climbed every week: 2.6, 5.2, 6.7, 15.4.

26. Malik Washington (vs. CIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

27. Josh Downs (vs. PIT)

28. Luther Burden III (at GB) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

29. Tre Tucker (at NE) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Ashton Jeanty has a foot injury, and CB1 Christian Gonzalez and CB2 Carlton Davis are out. Raiders WR2 Jalen Nailor is also out. Everything is breaking his way, and Tucker is good enough on film to be utilized under impressive HC Klint Kubiak.

30. DJ Moore (at LAR)

Moore is very questionable to play after DNP-DNP-limited practices this week, following last game's setback to his injured AC joint. It's a massive game with the Rams on Monday Night Football, and he has a 5+ season active game streak to play for, but the floor is low. The ceiling remains high as a fantasy WR3. Make sure to have either Keon Coleman or Khalil Shakir if holding out.

31. Carnell Tate (vs. HOU) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Tate was limited with a back injury in practice.

Tate had a career-high 15.8 expected half PPR points in Week 4 and his usage has climbed in three straight games. Results were mixed, but things are generally trending up. Cam Ward delivered a couple of wow throws out of structure to Tate, who was only targeted five+ yards downfield on all 12 of his looks. There were some high throws with offbeat timing in there, but the volume is real and there will be go-ball explosives eventually. He had a double-move penalty drawn on him from All-Pro S Kyle Hamilton as an example. Tate is the WR34 on WR22 usage to start his career, and I don't see Calvin Ridley, Wan'Dale Robinson and others eating into his alpha status.

32. Rome Odunze (at GB) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

33. Deebo Samuel Sr. (at SEA) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

34. Devaughn Vele (vs. MIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Vele is a real fantasy WR3. He became a full-time player in Week 12 last year, and he's the WR22 on WR17 usage in eight games since. This year, Vele is the WR21 on WR13 usage with Tyler Shough leading the NFL with 48 dropbacks per game. Only six other teams are above 40 for reference.

Vele's extreme catch radius comes in handy, as we saw with his toe-tapping garbage-time touchdown on Monday Night Football. He also has a goal-line fade as the lone WR on the field this season, and he's consistently targeted on breaking routes about 10 yards down the field. With Jordyn Tyson realistically targeting a Week 9 return, Vele is looking like a high-end rental.

35. Terry McLaurin (vs. NYG) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

36. Denzel Boston (at NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Severe rain is expected.

37. KC Concepcion (at NYJ) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Severe rain is expected.

38. Keon Coleman (at LAR) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: DJ Moore is questionable after DNP-DNP-limited practices. This assumes he's not himself, and Coleman slightly benefits. If Moore was out, Coleman is a top-30 WR.

39. Kendrick Bourne (vs. DET)

Update: Marvin Harrison Jr. (trade) is out, so Bourne will be up a slight tick in expected targets. We can't over-state the jump, however, as Harrison was rarely involved in the offense aside from on sideline go balls and red zone fades. Bourne's trust from LaFleur could make him a highly-targeted underneath threat in fast-paced games like this one.

40. Emeka Egbuka (at DAL) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Jalon Daniels was just fine in his debut as an undrafted free agent. That was the earliest into a rookie season that an UDFA QB has started a game. The Bucs tried to hide him with a season-low neutral pass rate, and Daniels is going to scramble around a bit, too. That said, Daniels has a live arm and is willing to sling it. There could be garbage-time production here. He's good enough for that.

Egbuka was only targeted three times last week, leading to a WR83 finish on WR66 usage. Playing him in fantasy is absolutely daring, as the Bucs made sure to get Chris Godwin Jr. and Cade Otton involved underneath more often. Egbuka is going to work downfield more than them, making it harder to find a floor. Egbuka hasn't been overly impressive on tape either, even if the offense is doing more creative things with him before and at the snap.

The Cowboys have the worst-graded zone defense this year, per PFF, if you're feeling risky or are just desperate. They've allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to WRs this year, most recently getting smoked by Nico Collins (WR3), Zay Flowers (104 yards on a couple dozen routes) and Stefon Diggs (WR8). The Cowboys will have new CB1 Joey Porter Jr. available for more snaps this week, and he'll very likely see Egbuka the most with Godwin hid in the slot more often. It's too much for me to bank on. The Bucs project for 19.5 points on the road.

41. Dontayvion Wicks (at JAX)

42. Jakobi Meyers (vs. PHI)

43. Courtland Sutton (at LAC) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

44. Roman Wilson (vs. IND) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

45. Chris Bell (vs. CIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

46. Wan'Dale Robinson (vs. HOU) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Wan'Dale is the WR41 on WR43 usage so far. He's not the full PPR scam that he was in previous OC Brian Daboll seasons, but he did have a screen, quick out and scramble-drill TD last week with Cam Ward playing a bit better than usual. There is still a lack of in-structure normalness from this pass game, leaving everyone floorless. Robinson also only ran a route on 71% of routes with Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley making this a 4-WR rotation behind alpha Carnell Tate.

47. Kalif Raymond (at GB) - 24.5 proj. receiving yards

48. Keenan Allen (at PIT) - 24.5 proj. receiving yards

49. Brian Thomas (vs. PHI)

50. Chris Godwin (at DAL)

51. Makai Lemon (at JAX)

52. Antonio Williams (vs. NYG) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

This assumes Terry McLaurin plays on a snap count, Stefon Diggs is out, and there is severe rain.

item.title: Mike Ditka was an American original who revolutionized football beyond Chicago | Opinion
item.description: Following Mike Ditka's death on Friday, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh shared a private moment that spoke volumes about the coach he loved to the bone.
item.content:encoded:
Opinion: Mike Ditka was an “American Original”

Jim Harbaugh, berated as QB on Bears sideline, reflects on another side of “Iron Mike”

Of all the tributes and testimonials, the statements, tweets and sound bites in the wake of Mike Ditka’s passing, nothing hit home for me like the reflections from Jim Harbaugh.

You see, long before Harbaugh became a coaching savant he was Ditka’s quarterback. And of all the images over many years that document Ditka’s presence as an NFL icon, there was that moment in 1992 when Harbaugh drew Iron Mike’s ire for the world to see.

With the Chicago Bears up 20-0 on the Vikings in the fourth quarter, Harbaugh audibled from the play sent in from the sideline and a bad thing happened. Harbaugh’s pass floated beyond intended receiver Neal Anderson and into the arms of Todd Scott, who turned the game around – Minnesota won 21-20 – with a pick-six.

Ditka went ballistic. When Harbaugh came to the sideline, Iron Mike berated him before a national TV audience. It was old-school, in-your-face fury. And if you loved the Bears, it was another reason to revere your coach.

More: Mike Ditka's defining coaching moments: Remembering the Bears legend

Harbaugh, the Bears first-round pick in 1987, held his usual Friday news conference as Los Angeles Chargers coach hours after Ditka’s family announced his passing at 86. As he reflected on his former coach there was no mention of that memory from the Metrodome.

No, Harbaugh’s memories are much better than that.

Instead, when someone asked him to share a favorite Ditka story, Harbaugh shared a private moment that spoke volumes about the coach he loved to the bone. He reflected on the time when Ditka called him into his office during the work week. Before they got around to the business of discussing the gameplan, Ditka had to finish up another task.

“He was writing out checks and signing checks,” Harbaugh said. “I could see that from across the desk.”

One check. Then another. And another.

“I finally said, ‘What are you doing, coach?’ ” Harbaugh recalled. “He had gotten a stack of letters. People in need. He was writing $500 checks to each.”

Harbaugh was stunned.

“Do you know these people?”

Ditka: “No, don’t know ’em.”

“That was all he said. He was never one to self-promote that,” Harbaugh added. “Just happened to witness it with my own eyes.”

Harbaugh was downright poetic as he reflected on the authentic coach that he loved to the bone, who reminded him of his father, Jack. He suggested that if anyone wanted to know Ditka’s essence, it could be found in Rudyard Kipling’s classic poem, If. Or with the slice of Teddy Roosevelt’s speech in 1910, known as “The Man in the Arena.”

“A true American hero,” Harbaugh said. “May he rest in peace.”

Exclusive: Mike Ditka commemorative book

Mike Ditka was Chicago

Ditka was Chicago, tried and true. Two decades after he broke into the NFL with the Bears as a first-round pick in 1961, he came back as head coach. It is fitting that Ditka led the franchise to its only Lombardi Trophy, which culminated with a Super Bowl 20 triumph for a team that might have been the greatest NFL champion ever. The ’85 Bears had so much swagger, so much personality – and a zany video, “The Super Bowl Shuffle” – and Ditka was perfect for keeping them on track for their special mission.

“Mike had a relationship with every player,” Jeff Fisher told The Tennessean, part of The USA TODAY Network, on Friday. A former safety, Fisher stuck as a seventh-round pick in 1981 and earned a Super Bowl ring while on injured reserve in 1985.

“He managed the personalities,” added Fisher, who went on to coach the Titans and Rams. “He let them unfold. He didn’t mold them. You have to be able to do that.”

The Bears flew the U.S. flag at half-staff at Halas Hall after Ditka’s passing and undoubtedly there will be moments of silence at other stadiums across the NFL on Sunday to commemorate one of the game’s legends.

Ditka was tried and true Pitt, too. He was a three-sport athlete – in addition to playing tight end and punting, he played forward on the basketball squad and outfield on the baseball team – at the University of Pittsburgh.

Mike Ditka's time with the Cowboys

For several years, he belonged to the Dallas Cowboys, too. He finished his 12-year NFL playing career as a player-coach and caught the last touchdown in the Super Bowl 6 win against Miami. Roger Staubach credited Ditka for his impact in bringing the team together as they meshed on their journey. Another player-coach on Tom Landry’s staff, Dan Reeves, said it was Ditka who suggested the Cowboys employ the shotgun formation that became a signature.

“He said, ‘It would give us a little more time. You know we got a quarterback who can scramble,'" Reeves once said, according to the team’s website.

During his stint as special teams coach on Landry’s staff for nine years, Ditka also provided a glimpse of his sideline fury. After Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Ron Johnson drew a flag for slamming Drew Pearson to the turf out of bounds, Ditka retaliated by hurling the football and hitting Johnson in the head. And drawing a flag.

Ditka belonged to the Saints, too. He went 15-33 during a three-year stint in New Orleans marked by the ill-advised decision to trade his entire package of 1999 draft picks – and first- and third-round picks the following year – for the right to select Heisman Trophy winner Ricky Williams with the fifth pick overall.

Ditka also belonged to ESPN as a studio analyst, a lightning rod on the air.

And let’s not forget. As much Ditka’s political leaning turns me off – “He was MAGA all the way,” Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform on Friday – there’s so much to respect about the way he championed the cause for medical benefits and financial assistance for retired players through his Gridiron Greats Assistance Fund.

That was pure Ditka. He may have been a cultural phenomenon, but beyond that he was the man Harbaugh saw writing out checks to people in need.

Of course, Ditka also belonged to the community he drew up in near Pittsburgh. Ditka was not only the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, he was also the first Hall of Famer from Aliquippa, Pennsylvania – followed by Tony Dorsett, Darrelle Revis and Ty Law.

Mike Ditka revolutionized the tight end position

Here’s to the mark that Ditka left on the game as a player. For so many years, he’s been revered as an OG, a classic throwback defined by his grit. Yet when he broke onto the NFL season 65 years ago, Ditka was so cutting edge.

Before Gronk and Tony Gonzalez, before Kellen Winslow, Ozzie Newsome and Travis Kelce, there was Ditka. George “Papa Bear” Halas sought to reimagine the tight end position when he drafted the consensus All-America pick with the fifth pick overall. Did he ever.

Ditka caught 56 passes for 1,076 yards and 12 TDs in 14 games as a rookie in 1961. By today’s standards, those numbers don’t jump off the page. But consider that until Winslow broke out in the Chargers’ “Air Coryell” system in 1980 to break Ditka’s 1964 tight end record of 75 receptions, just one other tight end (Jackie Smith, 1967) topped 1,000 yards. And Ditka’s mark for receiving yards by a rookie tight end wasn’t eclipsed until Brock Bowers came along for the Raiders in 2024.

“Mike brought competitiveness and a hard-nosed style of play as he developed into both a fantastic blocker and someone who could punish would-be tacklers on his receptions,” Jim Porter, executive director of the Pro Football of Fame, said in a statement.

No, Ditka was not to be messed with on so many levels.

It’s no wonder that Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell, who played tight end in the NFL for 11 seasons, reflected Friday with such reverence. Campbell said it was an awesome experience, but also one of the most “intimidating” moments of his life when he met Ditka, then the Saints coach, for a one-on-one session during the NFL combine in 1999.

“I go in and there’s one little light on,” Campbell recalled during a news conference at Lions headquarters. “It's like a little lamp in the corner, you know? It's at the train station and there's nothing in there. There's no couches there. The room is totally cleaned out and there's one little table and the room is full of smoke.”

Campbell said he could barely see the legend as he conducted the interview.

“You just see this image off in the corner…and he’s got that big fat cigar,” Campbell said.

Classic Ditka.

There’s no blueprint for what it takes to become an American Original. You know it when you see it. In Mike Ditka, we saw it unequivocally, during his storybook life and career. He created the mold and broke it. And there will never be one another one quite like him.

The Eagles running back depth got even thinner on Sunday morning, when Will Shipley left the game shortly after scoring the team’s first touchdown in London. The RB was evaluated on the sideline before leaving for the locker room late in the second quarter, and was listed as questionable to return due to a foot injury.

Shipley came into the Week 5 game as the starter due to Saquon Barkley inactive due to a hamstring injury, and Tank Bigsby on IR after undergoing core muscle surgery. The team signed running backs Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele from the practice squad to the roster earlier this week.

In addition to the touchdown, Shipley had five carries for six yards before leaving the game. His contributions aren’t just on offense, and the team will have to fill his spot on special teams, too.

Thankfully, the Eagles passing game looked improved — at least a little — in the first half, and hopefully they are able to cobble together a competent performance in the second half and squeak out a win.

item.title: The Cowboys coaching decision no one is talking about
item.description: Should the Cowboys have let Brandon Aubrey attempt a 64-yard field goal on Thursday night?
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys lost on Thursday night. It remains incredibly frustrating.

If I asked you for the most contentious decision that the coaching staff made in the process, you would likely bring up the decision that Brian Schottenheimer made to go for two when down by eight in the fourth quarter. This particular author supported that for what it’s worth, just about the only thing I endorsed from Schottenheimer throughout the loss.

While that decision has inspired a lot of responses there is another Cowboys coaching decision that merits discussion. This one came much earlier in the game.

Almost halfway through the second quarter, Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb failed to connect on a 3rd and 10. It was 4th and 10, obviously, and the Cowboys chose to punt.

The thing is the Cowboys were on the Tampa Bay 47-yard line. They turned down a 64-yard field goal attempt, something that Brandon Aubrey is regarded to be very good at.

Aubrey hasn’t exactly been super reliable on these as of late, though. He had a 59-yard attempt blocked by the Baltimore Ravens, and a week later he had a 62-yard attempt blocked by the Houston Texans. Schottenheimer also chose to have Aubrey attempt a 65-yarder against Houston on the possession after the block and he missed it outright. In the week after the game, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans talked about how they were partly able to block the kick they did because of something they saw on film from Dallas’ game against Baltimore.

You never want to see this kind of thing. It looks bad on the Cowboys, it looks bad on Schottenheimer, and it specifically looks bad on special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen.

Did those two blocks occupy some rent in the Cowboys’ minds on the decision to not let Aubrey attempt the 64-yarder against Tampa? It is hard to say not. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram’s Nick Harris pulled the last time that Dallas punted from across the 50-yard line and it was midway through last year, but the last time they punted from inside of the 47-yard line specifically was late in the 2024 season. It is worth noting that by that time in that season Dak Prescott was out for the year already so the calculus was a bit different.

To be clear, it is impossible to say with full certainty that the Cowboys punted because of a lack of faith in any one person or side of the ball. But it is certainly a legitimate theory. That particular decision was hardly costly. The Buccaneers went on the punt themselves so there was no blood drawn.

But what if Aubrey had attempted the 64-yard attempt? What if he had made it? Then the Cowboys could have gone for two when they did in an effort to make the game (at that time) a three-point contest. And if they had gotten it, they didn’t get it as we all know, then they would have only needed a field goal to tie at the end of regulation. That is a lot of ifs and hypotheticals, but they rest on the decision that Dallas made to not have Brandon Aubrey attempt the field goal.

What do you think? Was it a lack of faith? Or something random?

item.title: Vikings' touchdown drought isn't keeping them from winning
item.description: The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters.
item.content:encoded:
The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters. And the stout defense isn't getting a ton of help from the offense.

The Vikings have had 18 straight drives without a touchdown. The last one happened in the second quarter of a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers. The Week 4 victory over the Dolphins happened with five field goals.

Yes, tight end T.J. Hockenson could have scored just before the two-minute warning, but he wisely took a knee and allowed the Vikings to ensure the Dolphins wouldn't be able to score twice and steal the game. Either way, the Vikings did not register a touchdown against the Dolphins.

As noted last Sunday, the win made the Vikings the first team in more than 100 years to start 4-0 despite not scoring a touchdown in multiple games. The 1922 and 1923 Chicago Cardinals were the only other teams to accomplish that feat.

If the Vikings do it again at any point this year, they'll become only the fourth team in NFL history to win three or more games without scoring a touchdown. The others were the 1922 Chicago Cardinals, the 1923 Chicago Bears, and the 1993 Indianapolis Colts, per NBC Sports research.

The all-time record, held by the 1922 Cardinals, is four.

Still, there's reason to believe the Vikings could snap out of their early-season funk. After the Dolphins scored a touchdown late in the third quarter to cut Minnesota's lead to 12-10, the Vikings offense seemed to wake up. A 15-play, 60-yard drive consumed more than eight minutes of clock time and extended the lead to 15-10. Then, after a three-and-out effort from the Dolphins, the Vikings burned the remaining 5:41 by moving the ball 79 yards from their own 19 to the Miami two.

The next test comes today, in New Orleans. The 1-3 Saints are desperate for a win after losing their first two home games of the season — capped by Monday night's embarrassing loss to the Falcons. New Orleans hasn't lost its first three games at home since 1995.

item.content:encoded:
The primetime spotlight on "Sunday Night Football" will shine on the Atlanta Falcons and the Baltimore Ravens, and quarterback Lamar Jackson's injury status has been in question all week.

Jackson injured his ankle in the second quarter of a Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans when Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson tackled him, landing his shoulder on Jackson's left ankle.

Fortunately, the Ravens didn't need him, and they hung on to win 24-18 to improve to 3-1.

Jackson was 15-for-20 for 222 passing yards and two touchdowns, and added 20 yards on the ground before leaving the game.

For Sunday's game in Atlanta, linebacker Trey Hendrickson and center Cam Jurgens, who was traded from the Philadelphia Eagles this week, will also miss the game.

"To Lamar's credit, this dude's working his tail off to get back," Minter said. "He's in there all the time. Don't know the specifics of next week, but he'll be doing everything in his power to get back."

This season, Jackson is completing 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, with six touchdowns and one interception, and has added 144 rushing yards with one score.

Jackson will be replaced in the starting lineup Sunday night by Tyler Huntley, who has a 5-6 career record with the Ravens.

"We've got a ton of confidence in Snoop," Minter said. "He played really well. I think everybody on the team is excited to see that and him to have this opportunity."

  • Joe Fagnano

item.title: Bears to honor legendary coach Mike Ditka with No. 89 helmet decal
item.description: The Bears will continue to honor Mike Ditka.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears will make sure they honor legendary coach Mike Ditka in Week 5. Ditka — who led the Bears to a win in Super Bowl XX — died Friday. He was 86.

In tribute to Ditka, the team unveiled a helmet decal featuring No. 89, the number Ditka wore when he was a tight end with the franchise. The Bears retired the number in 2013, and team chairman George McCaskey said it will be the last number the Bears ever retire.

The decal will appear on the back of the team's helmet, just under the American flag.

For 89 💙 pic.twitter.com/0pynPgHoBb

— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 11, 2026

While Ditka is arguably more known for his stint as a head coach, he began his legend as a tight end with the Bears. He is credited with redefining the position, becoming one of the first tight ends to be used as a major receiving threat.

In his six seasons with the Bears, Ditka made five Pro Bowls and was a two-time first team All-Pro selection. He gained 4,503 receiving yards and scored 34 touchdowns with the franchise. Ditka later played for both the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys.

His excellence as a player got him inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame while he was still coaching.

As a coach, Ditka excelled with the Bears. In 11 seasons with the franchise, he posted a .631 winning percentage and won a Super Bowl. Following his time in Chicago, Ditka coached the New Orleans Saints, where he went 15-33 in three seasons.

His excellence as both a player and coach, combined with his outspoken personality, made Ditka a popular figure in the game, even after his retirement. Because of that, a number of individuals paid tribute to Ditka on Friday.

The Bears will add one more tribute to that list Sunday.

item.title: New York Jets: A more disciplined defense is missing less tackles
item.description: The Jets defense is wrapping up more this season
item.content:encoded:
Missed tackles. They are a frustrating fact of life in the NFL. Every team misses multiple tackles per game, but some are worse offenders than others. The New York Jets have been egregious in this fundamental facet of the game for years.

Different sites will give slightly different figures. Working with Pro Football Reference numbers, the Jets have been among the NFL’s least efficient tackling teams. In the six years from 2020 through 2025 the Jets ranked in the top half of the NFL just once, and they ranked in the bottom six four times. Yikes! That’s not good. Here are the Jets rankings in the NFL in missed tackles since 2020:

2025 – 27th

2024 – 28th

2023 – 24th

2022 – 14th

2021 – 27th

2020 – 30th

2026 has been a different story thus far. The Jets have missed just 17 tackles in their first four games this season. That number makes them the NFL’s 10th best team in tackling. Bringing in sound tacklers appears to have been a Jets priority in the 2026 offseason, and it is paying dividends early this season. We have seen more wrapping up and less rolling into guys with the shoulder this season. It’s been great to see, but surprisingly it is a bit difficult to find much correlation in missed tackles to a team’s record.

Three of the top six teams this season in missed tackles are the Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins. They have combined for a 1-11 record this season. In fact, of the top ten teams in 2026 for missed tackles, just two teams have a winning record.

Going back to 2025, seven of the top 16 teams in missed tackles had losing records. It is a somewhat puzzling thing, but missed tackles don’t appear to be much of a factor in wins and losses. Nonetheless, if given a choice, a team would certainly prefer not to miss tackles. For the first time in a long while, the Jets have actually been good at this. If nothing else, it makes the defense more fun to watch. Perhaps it also is a leading indicator that the Jets are finally instilling a more disciplined approach on a team that has been badly in need of it for years. It may not amount to a big deal, but perhaps it’s a small silver lining in what has been a disappointing start to the Aaron Glenn era.

item.title: Rams special teams would get boost from this practice squad player
item.description: Promoting Presley to the active roster would bolster the L.A. Rams return game
item.content:encoded:
What if the Los Angeles Rams had a player with a long history of both punt and kickoff returns, that at the risk of being over dramatic, is just languishing on the practice squad? Brennan Presley is on the Rams’ practice squad and he could be the answer to rekindle some explosivity to their return game if they call him up.

It is only Week 5 and the L.A. special teams unit is already in disarray. It’s not a new topic, it feels like a year-to-year discussion since Sean McVay parted ways with John Fassell after the 2019 season. Fans have been weighing in on the current regime since early spring and TST has had plenty to say about it.

The Rams coverage units are 30th in punt return average allowed (14.4) and 22nd in kickoffs (27.0). Return units rank 18th for punts (9.0) and 31st in kickoffs (21.9).

While the Rams have made a concerted effort to shore up leaky coverage with outside players, they don’t appear to have done the same due diligence in the return game.

Signed by the Rams in 2025, out of the undrafted ranks. 24 years old and diminutive in stature, 5’ 8” 175 lb. Left Oklahoma State at or towards the top of their all-time receiving, all-purpose and return lists

Since he didn’t get into a regular season game in 2025, to grade and project Presley, fans have to go by his work and numbers from college days at Oklahoma State. He started in 44 of 63 games played and left as OSU’s all-time leader in pass receptions and towards the top in all receiving categories, chalking up 315 catches for 3315 yards and 23 scores. To compliment those receiving yards, he averaged over 1000 yards per season in all-purpose production, chipping in 160 yards rushing, 1427 in kickoff return yardage, and 240 yards on punt returns.

Presley posted strong athletic testing numbers at the Big 12 Pro Day. To go along with very good long speed (4.46) he  showed plus burst, balance, flexibility, change of direction (6.71 shuttle) and short-area agility (4.07 3cone) to go along with very good long speed. His ability to run with the ball stands out. A jitterbug style with slippery-fast change of direction and makes his cuts at speed. If given sliver of space, he seems to always beat the first tackler, played running back in high school and runs with willing physicality for a small player.

Presley is not what I would grade as a “can’t miss” returner, but does bring the right skillset and background. His darting open-field style hasn’t been seen a pro game, but he’s looked solid in preseason work. Because of his ability with ball in his hands, he does double duty as a receiver and his traits carry over to both. Oklahoma State flooded him with a lot of short/mid  range routes to utilize that advantage. He was predominantly a slot receiver, but also saw reps outside, in bunch sets, and in motion. He came to L.A. needing to expand his route tree, but showed off good hands, ball tracking, and body control to reel in imperfect passes. Like most small receivers, he’ll need to adjust physical press coverage and could have issues at the catch point against bigger, longer secondary players. He does have a good feel for soft areas in zones and works back to his quarterback when flushed from the pocket.

At a very good price, Presley can wear a lot of hats as a versatile special teams piece piece to go along with work on offense. In fact, during his first three college seasons, he not only worked as a returner, but played on coverage units as a gunner as well. He was lauded by coaches for his work ethic, leadership and competitive juices.

Are the Rams ready/willing to make this decision?

Probably not. Just a week ago, we fans found out how much weight should be given to what L.A. special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone offers on the unit’s progress, or lack thereof.. In a 10/1 Thursday presser, Ventrone gave Xavier Smith, the Rams primary punt returner for three seasons, his public support and 24 hours later, the XMan was jettisoned. While very few fans would disagree with the move, how the Rams handled it does cause some raised eyebrows. Sean McVay wasted no time in naming Alex Bachman as the new returner, deep on both kickoffs and punts.

In all fairness, grading Bachman on one game is a tiny sample, but the film of the Eagle game left a lot to be desired. After nine seasons, his only playing in 24 total games, with 27 punt returns (22 last year) and eight kickoff returns doesn’t inspire much confidence. Last Sunday, I offered six candidates for the Rams return game and said this about the Rans decision to install Bachman as of now, the primary kick returner,

“…I have to wonder how many would consider this move an upgrade. Although Bachman fielded a fair amount of kicks for the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he does not have a history as a returner., nor is he known as an open-field runner. His production was only mediocre It appears a lateral move, at best.”

The Rams need to see what they’ve got with Brennan Presley. The status quo is not making anything better.

It's concerning that without Alec Pierce and Keenan Allen last week, Warren could only muster up five scoreless receptions for 41 yards as the TE21 overall. The offense won't generate many pass-game explosives with their style, and the OL has regressed versus their peak a few seasons ago. Warren will always be a short-area dominant player without the high-end speed and fluidity of the truly elite TEs. That's okay if we keep expectations in check. He's the TE13 on TE8 usage this year, even with injuries breaking his way.

8. Colston Loveland (at GB) - 37.5 proj. yards

Loveland has unfortunately gone under his usage-based expected points in four straight games. He's turned TE13 usage into just TE38 fantasy points per game because he hasn't converted his red-zone targets into touchdowns. His route share is also 10-20% lower than the truly elite TEs right now and faces more target competition than everyone else at the position. Loveland is too good for this to hold, but he does only have a 15% target share and 21 air yards per game right now. The Bears are projected for 24.0 points (ninth) with Tyson Bagent at QB, and the Packers just placed LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles) on IR. This is the first time they've faced a fantasy-relevant TE this season.

9. Oronde Gadsden II (vs. DEN)

Update: Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston are expected to miss, leaving Gadsden and Tre' Harris as the only pass catchers with real experience with Justin Herbert. The Broncos are missing key starters in the secondary and their LBs have been picked on for a bulk of the season. This is the best he's look pre-game since his wild fantasy TE1 stint in the middle of last year.

10. T.J. Hockenson (at NO)

Update: I'm projecting Justin Jefferson (ankle) to play, while Jordan Addison (hamstring) misses. This is still up in the air, however.

Hockenson's 18.4 expected half PPR points in Week 4 were his most since 2023 Week 10, and it's obviously not a coincidence that it happened without Justin Jefferson (ankle). Hockenson was an outlet and quick first read up the seam against an inexperienced Dolphins defense, but with the WR group underwhelming, he's looking more intriguing than ever. The warning is he's not a big-play threat, and the Vikings are 29th in neutral pass rate right now. He's best treated as a low-end TE1 even after what was likely his season-high game.

11. Isaiah Likely (at WAS) - 40.5 proj. yards

Likely is the TE8 on TE4 usage this season, and Jameis Winston clearly has eyes on him. Likely had 15.5 expected half PPR points (TE5) last week, while being targeted underneath on first reads and downfield on prayers. Winston's decision-making, accuracy and arm strength remain suspect to me, but we're chasing volume and Likely has a section of the call sheet carved out for him. His 31% target share leads the position, so all it takes is the Giants to get in negative game script to take off.

The matchup is also good. The Commanders have allowed Dallas Goedert (TE2), Jake Ferguson (TE4) and AJ Barner (69 yards) spike weeks this season. They've been a pass funnel unit so far, allowing just 94 rushing YPG (27th) versus 255 passing YPG (eighth).

12. Juwan Johnson (vs. MIN) - 42.5 proj. yards

Johnson is the TE4 on TE5 usage this season, and he's been at least the TE14 in usage in all four games this season. In 15 games with Tyler Shough dating back to last year, Johnson is averaging 9.9 half PPR points (TE7). He's made countless plays after the catch this season, and the Saints didn't have Noah Fant (abs) active on Monday Night Football, leading to a 75% route rate. That's slightly up from 72% and 62%.

The Week 5 matchup is what is holding him back. The Saints only project for 20.5 points against the chaotic Vikings defense. I'm not sure if their new (struggling) LT is ready, and teams haven't cracked the code with TEs against DC Brian Flores. Colston Loveland nearly had a goose egg back in Week 2, while every other TE has gone scoreless on limited receptions.

13. Dallas Goedert (at JAX)

14. Mark Andrews (at ATL) - 29.5 proj. yards

15. Harold Fannin Jr. (at NYJ) - 36.5 proj. yards

Update: Severe rain is in the forecast.

Fannin's Week 1 dud feels like a long time ago at this point. He's the TE9 on TE12 usage this year with back-to-back top-10 outings. The Browns are quietly second in neutral pass rate right now, as new HC Todd Monken has adapted to his personnel yet again. It's the way to play it for them, and it's going to help Fannin hold onto TE1/2 relevance even if Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are screaming upgrades to Fannin's competition as a record-setting rookie. The Jets are better at defending TEs than WRs so far if we want to nitpick the matchup, but there's no real reason to be nervous with Fannin's individual projection.

16. Dalton Schultz (at TEN) - 37.5 proj. yards

17. Hunter Henry (vs. LV) - 37.5 proj. yards

18. Jake Ferguson (vs. TB) - 26.5 proj. yards

19. Tyler Higbee (vs. BUF)

Higbee has been the TE3 and TE18 in usage over the past two weeks as the clear-cut top receiving option in the group with Terrence Ferguson on IR. He turned six targets into 67 yards last week in a difficult road matchup, and now the Rams are at home on Monday Night Football against a struggling Bills defense. There are worse thrown darts.

20. Kenyon Sadiq (vs. CLE) - 32.5 proj. yards

Update: Severe rain is in the forecast, and Mason Taylor is back.

With the Jets only playing 32 snaps of offense (fourth fewest in a single game in NFL history, folks), Sadiq busted. He didn't catch any of his four targets, while playing 69% of snaps and running 67% of routes. He was the TE4 on TE9 usage in Week 3 without Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor, however.

21. Pat Freiermuth (vs. IND) - 27.5 proj. yards

22. Brenton Strange (vs. PHI) - 33.5 proj. yards

23. Michael Mayer (at NE) - 28.5 proj. yards

24. AJ Barner (vs. SF) - 23.5 proj. yards

25. Kyle Pitts Sr. (vs. BAL) - 24.5 proj. yards

Pitts is the TE27 on TE22 usage in his 14 career games with Michael Penix Jr., who has peppered Drake London with a wild 35% target share. That held true on Monday Night Football when Pitts had three targets (mostly off play action) as a rotational player. He only ran a route on 10-of-22 dropbacks.

Speaking of drops, Pitts is droppable in fantasy as the TE50 on TE49 usage. He should be thought of as London insurance. He would flirt with top-eight fantasy scores, if not higher, if London misses at any point. We're done here until proven otherwise.

26. Chig Okonkwo (vs. NYG) - 27.5 proj. yards

27. Cade Otton (at DAL) - 29.5 proj. yards

28. Darnell Washington (vs. IND) - 22.5 proj. yards

29. Mike Gesicki (at MIA)

Update: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) have a chance to play.

On top of that, the Bengals are facing the worst defense in the NFL this week. Miami allowed T.J. Hockenson to go for 119 yards last week, and both Travis Kelce and George Kittle have generated massive plays with separate scores, too. It's been three straight outings allowing a top-eight TE for the Dolphins.

30. Evan Engram (at LAC) - 17.5 proj. yards
