item.title: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. ejected from Eagles-Jaguars game
item.description: The Eagles are down a linebacker just 13 seconds into their Week 5 game against the Jags.
item.content:encoded:
Well, things escalated for the Eagles in London.

Even though the Eagles already have a thin roster, they’ll be without linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who was ejected in the first 13 seconds of the game.

The Eagles kicked things off to start the game, and the Jaguars returned the kick 91 yards for a touchdown. Thankfully, offsetting penalties required a re-kick, but not before Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Bryan Thomas Jr. were ejected for fighting at mid-field.

Fortunately, Zack Baun is back for the Eagles defense this week, after he missed last week’s game due to a concussion, so the team still has some depth at linebacker. Still, it’s not ideal for the team, or for Trotter, who had a really good game last week. DC Vic Fangio even said that the LB possibly earned some more playing time after he performance, but that was cut short on Sunday in London.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 5
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks reveals his Week 5 running back rankings in the Blueprint.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column on Thursdays and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (at ARI) - 132.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs has 105.1 half PPR points through four weeks. That's RB14 all-time. He's unsurprisingly the RB1 on RB1 overall usage this season, with 20.0+ expected half PPR points every week.

2. Bijan Robinson (vs. BAL) - 122.5 proj. total yards

Bijan has scored 25+ half PPR points in 7-of-10 recent games. In 14 games with Michael Penix Jr. dating back to late 2024, Bijan is averaging 22.9 half-PPR points on 5.1 targets per game. He didn't need to be thrown the ball on Monday Night Football because the ground game was on absolute fire. The Falcons' OL was moving bodies, and Bijan's effortless speed and elite cutback ability sent him to an RB5 overall finish. He's the RB3 on RB5 usage this year while battling with Jahmyr Gibbs, Kenneth Walker III and Jonathan Taylor for the top spots in rankings each week.

The Ravens are a solid defense, but they've been vulnerable to fantasy RBs so far. Tony Pollard (RB24), Javonte Williams (RB10) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8) all had games in line with their averages. Baltimore is allowing the 21st-most fantasy points per game to RBs on 100 yards per game. The Falcons are projected for 23.5 points (11th), which I believe is the highest of the year for them.

3. Kyren Williams (vs. BUF) - 94.5 proj. total yards

Williams is icing Blake Corum more in 2026 than he did down the stretch last year, particularly whenever the Rams are trailing or smell a mismatch with opposing LBs. He caught 10 balls last week while chasing points in the second half, and he's been a trusted asset in both phases (aside from those lingering fumbles). Williams is the RB6 on RB9 usage so far, but he's improved his totals every week. Last week's 28.0 expected half PPR points (RB1 overall) were a career high. Dog.

The Bills and Rams combine for a 54.5-point game total. I've been impressed by the Bills' DTs when they've been available and very underwhelmed by their back half with CB1 Christian Benford also banged up. Buffalo isn't a defense to shy away from, even if outlier-sized DT Deone Walker is looking like a Pro Bowler next to Ed Oliver. The Bills allowed 16.9+ half PPR points to Rhamondre Stevenson (RB13), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and David Montgomery (RB6) so far. Even Keaton Mitchell was the RB14 in Week 3.

4. Jonathan Taylor (at PIT) - 108.5 proj. total yards

Taylor's 2026 value has been nearly identical to last year's with Daniel Jones active. His half PPR points per game are down by just 2.2, and his expected points based on his elite role are actually up 0.7 year-over-year. He has a career-low 4.1 YPC right now, for no fault of his own, but his targets per game are at a career high to counter it. The Colts' upside won't hit without a real downfield threat, and I'm not sure it's going to matter for JT's top-5 RB status. He's the RB5 on RB7 usage this year despite already facing the Ravens, Chiefs, Texans and underrated Commanders defenses.

The Steelers have headliners across the defensive line, but they've been gashed by fantasy RBs so far. Bijan Robinson had his usual 27.3 half PPR points (RB7) in Week 1, followed by a long TD run to TreVeyon Henderson (RB9) in Week 2 and a career-high 6-reception game from Quinshon Judkins (RB11) last week. The Colts are projected for 21.0 points (19th) after getting a bit exposed at RT in recent outings.

5. D'Andre Swift (at GB) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Update: Kyle Monangai (toe) is likely to miss.

Swift was benched after his third-quarter fumble while Kyle Monangai ran the hot hand. It happens, but no, I don't think this holds after Swift has balled out this season following his September multi-year contract extension. The Bears are splitting up a league-leading 30.8 expected half PPR points between these two, and that upside needs to be respected at all times, even coming off duds. Swift is the RB12 on RB8 usage this season.

A matchup with the Packers is a solid one. The Bears project for 24.25 points (10th) with Tyson Bagent expected back under center. Green Bay has allowed the second-most fantasy points to RBs this season on 139 rushing yards per game (fifth). Bijan Robinson dropped a clean 34.3 half PPR points in Week 3, while Breece Hall (RB13) and Jordan Mason (RB20) had productive days earlier. Swift had three games against them late last year, posting 16.2, 8.0 and 9.7 half PPR points in Weeks 19, 16 and 14.

6. Jaylen Warren (vs. IND)

Warren is the RB14 and RB16 in usage without Rico Dowdle, and he's looked quite good on tape each game. The Steelers have found their best combination across the offensive line, and Aaron Rodgers has berated HC Mike McCarthy enough to find the sweet spot of the playbook, too. Dowdle said he dislocated his toe twice in Week 2 and is still waiting to work back to practice, so we can assume he'll miss another game here. Warren is the RB11 on RB15 usage in the past two weeks.

The Steelers are projected for 23.5 points (12th) against the Colts, who have had real issues defensively this season. Indianapolis has allowed the fifth-most pass yards per game (276) and seventh-most rush yards per game (131), despite facing the Commanders QB3 and the Texans without Nico Collins this season.

7. Javonte Williams (vs. TB) - 92.5 proj. total yards

Williams has quietly been one of the best picks in fantasy, as the RB7 on RB6 usage overall who was often available early in Round 4. He's the RB7 in receptions per game (3.8) while soaking up a ton of goal-line reps in this elite offense. Through four weeks, the Cowboys are top-five in points per drive since 2000.

The Buccaneers haven't faced a serious fantasy RB and offense in a bit, with recent games against the Packers, Vikings and Browns. The only thing to care about is the Cowboys' team total, which sits at 28.0 points (third). Everything else sorts itself out.

8. James Cook III (at LAR) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Cook averaged 16.0 half PPR points last year and is at 15.9 this year. Nothing has changed. He's the RB37 in receptions per game (1.5) but more than makes up for it by averaging 17.5 carries and 105 rush YPG on the most stable offense in the NFL. He's the RB11 on RB12 usage in 2026 as a mid- to low-end RB1 depending on the matchup.

The Bills are projected for 25.75 points (fourth) on Monday Night Football, in what easily could be the highest-scoring game of the week versus the Rams. The Rams have allowed the fewest fantasy points to RBs this season, with only Christian McCaffrey (88) eclipsing 55 total scoreless yards. But, and with all due respect, the Bills are a totally different beast than the Eagles, Broncos and Giants.

9. Christian McCaffrey (at SEA) - 93.5 proj. total yards

CMC had cramps in Australia in Week 1, and since then, he's the RB7 on RB9 usage. He's averaging his usual 4.0 receptions per game (RB6) and is RB3 in inside the five-yard line carries. All of the high-value touches are going his way, even if Kaelon Black is going to steal some snaps.

The 49ers are projected for 22.0 points (17th) this week despite a red-hot start because of this truly elite Seahawks defense. CMC has faced HC Mike Macdonald four times and scored 9.9, 8.7, 18.7, and 12.6 half PPR points (avg: 12.5) without a score. Seattle hasn't allowed a back to reach 100 total yards or 12.5 half PPR points this season either.

10. Chase Brown (at MIA) - 64.5 proj. total yards

Update: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have a chance to play now.

Brown is the ultimate buy-low right now. He's faced the Jaguars, Texans, Steelers and Bucs so far. From 2025 to now, those are the first-, fourth-, sixth- and 13th-best defenses against fantasy RBs. Brown is not talented enough to break out against the top competition, which is why he's the RB18 on RB11 usage so far. He's held the line with 5.3 receptions per game, but Brown will have far better raw numbers for the rest of the year.

The Bengals have been first in neutral pass rate this season by a wide margin, but they should run more in Week 5 against the Dolphins based on game script and WR injury. Miami has allowed three top-five fantasy RB finishers this season already and its fourth opponent was Aaron Jones Sr., who posted 128 total yards as the RB18. Brown had 30.9 fantasy points against the Dolphins in Week 16 of last year, too. Cincy is projected for 24.75 points (sixth).

11. Aaron Jones Sr. (at NO) - 95.5 proj. total yards

Jones has been a top-24 RB in every week, including RB18, RB15 and RB18 finishes in the most recent weeks as the Vikings' bellcow. Only 1 of 20 carries last week went for a negative, and Minnesota's offense is 29th in neutral pass rate right now. It's pretty much the Jones Show with Jordan Mason (IR) and potentially Justin Jefferson (ankle) out again. The hard part is squaring how uncomfortable the offense has been in general and with the new loss of LG Donovan Jackson. Jones' seasonal average of being the RB20 on RB16 usage seems like a fair starting point.

The Saints are on a short week after getting shredded by the Falcons' RB duo on Monday Night Football. They had 19 missed tackles in that one, and it wasn't just that game. They've allowed six RBs to reach 10+ half PPR points in four games. That's hard to do. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB4), Derrick Henry (RB7), Mike Washington Jr. (RB18), Ashton Jeanty (RB20), Bijan Robinson (RB5) and Brian Robinson Jr. (RB8) have all been top-20 backs. It's a good spot to catch them. Minnesota projects for 22.0 points (16th).

12. Derrick Henry (at ATL) - 94.5 proj. total yards

This assumes Lamar Jackson (ankle) is out with the Ravens' team total sitting at just 20.0 points (23rd). Henry has four games without Lamar Jackson in Baltimore, and he's passed the test with flying colors. He's averaged 21.9 half PPR points on 24 carries per game. There's simply not enough depth around Henry to move away from him in terms of elite total volume. The Big Dog has also been semi-involved as a receiver (RB31 receptions per game) to manage his floor, but Tyler Huntley starting behind this extremely injured interior OL is certainly playing with fire.

The Falcons defense has shown up despite missing arguably their top-three players. They've allowed the third-fewest fantasy points to RBs so far with Jaylen Warren, Chuba Hubbard and all Packers RBs going under their seasonal averages. Alvin Kamara plunged into the end zone a few times in Week 4 but on only 58 total yards. They haven't allowed 75 total yards to a running back this season.

13. Emanuel Wilson (vs. SF) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Wilson has handled 64% of the runs without Jadarian Price on the field this season, while Wilson and George Holani have split passing duties. Wilson caught three passes last week, including a screen TD and Holani had three pretty bad pass-protection mistakes. The "thunder" was the RB6 on RB15 usage last week. We should feel more confident than ever that Wilson will get a huge chunk of the Seahawks RB value for the next month, and they have 24.8 expected half PPR points per game (fourth) up for grabs based on the first four weeks:

The Week 5 matchup is a neutral one. The 49ers have so many defensive linemen out, including Nick Bosa, to trust to stop the run. They've allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to RBs this year, including top-20 finishes from RJ Harvey (RB20), Jeremiyah Love (RB7), De'Von Achane (RB16) and Kyren Williams (RB16). Backs have been catching passes in the flats often in this matchup, partially when the game is scoreboard-driven. That's not Wilson's specialty but he caught the ball cleanly last week. Seattle has a 24.5-point team total (ninth) as slight home favorites.

14. Braelon Allen (vs. CLE) - 91.5 proj. total yards

Update: Severe rain is in the forecast.

The Jets had 32 plays in Week 4. That's the fourth-fewest in NFL history. Yikes!!! The good news is Allen played 30-of-32 snaps without Breece Hall. His RB28 expected half PPR points (10.3), 14 carries and two receptions are essentially his floor without Hall. The Jets RB room has averaged 17.7 expected half PPR points this year, and 90% of that is a baseline of 15.0-16.0 fantasy points. It's very easy to make the math work as a fantasy RB2.

The matchup with the Browns is just fine. The Browns won't have 2025 fifth-overall pick DT Mason Graham, nor do they have an offense that's capable of dramatically winning the time of possession battle like the Bears did last week. RB starters against the Browns have cleared 88 total yards in all four outings, and they haven't been superstar talents: Bhayshul Tuten (RB25), Bucky Irving (RB15), Chuba Hubbard (RB12) and Jaylen Warren (RB21). Those rankings would be better if any of them had scored a touchdown. The Jets have a 21.0-point team total (21st).

15. Quinshon Judkins (at NYJ) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Update: Severe rain is in the forecast.

Judkins set career highs in expected half PPR points (22.9, RB4), targets (seven) and receptions (six) in Week 4 without Dylan Sampson. He added his usual 17 carries for 53 yards on the ground, but if this new receiving volume sticks under new HC Todd Monken's No. 2 neutral pass rate offense, then we may be underrating his value. He hasn't hit many explosives on the ground behind this gelling offensive line, but he is a capable runner who should be getting his feet back from under him after a gruesome ankle injury last year. Deshaun Watson scrambling for a first down and playing more composed has helped at the margins, too. Judkins is the RB24 on RB13 usage this season, unfortunately finishing below his expectation in seven straight games dating back to last year.

The Jets have allowed the most fantasy points to RBs when adjusting for opponent. Teams give their RBs 3.6 more carries per game against the Jets than their season average, and the Jets don't have the front seven to stop it. They've allowed 124 rush YPG, including 232 last week to the Bears and 164 to Jahmyr Gibbs in Week 3. If there's a game for Judkins to pop off on the ground, it's this one. The Browns are projected for just 18.5 points, though, so keep expectations in check.

16. Cam Skattebo (at WAS) - 76.5 proj. total yards

Update: Rainy conditions improve Skattebo's touch projection.

On the season, Skattebo is the RB26 on RB19 usage. He is feeling more pressure from Najee Harris than we'd like. His 49% route share from last week should lead to more targets moving forward, but he was the RB35 on RB31 usage in Week 4.

At one point, the Giants scored a TD (Theo Johnson) with Skattebo on the field, then they successfully ran in the 2-point conversion with subbed-in Harris. That was the lone goal-line opportunity of the game. Harris did brutally fumble the ball early in the fourth quarter, however, and was benched for the rest of the game. Harris also ran the ball himself on 10-of-12 snaps. Wild stuff here.

This matchup is a sneaky tough one under new DC Daronte Jones. The Commanders have allowed the 28th-most fantasy points to RBs, but that's fourth best when adjusting for opponent. They held a healthy Saquon Barkley to 8.5 half PPR points and Javonte Williams to just 6.5 earlier this season. With the Giants projected for 20.0 points (24th), Skattebo is more of an upside FLEX than a bankable RB2.

17. Ashton Jeanty (at NE) - 85.5 proj. total yards

Update: Jeanty is a game-time decision with a new toe injury, and the Raiders called up a practice-squad RB on Saturday as insurance. It's worth docking him in projections even if he suits up, which is truly up in the air. Mike Washington Jr. would be a fringe top-15 RB if Jeanty is out.

Jeanty played 74% of the first three drives in Weeks 1-3, then 43% last week. It's unclear if HC Klint Kubiak was attempting to find his hot hand or if there was another factor at play, but that was odd usage early on. By the fourth quarter, it went almost exclusively back to Jeanty when the Raiders were down multiple scores. It's very clear that Jeanty isn't just their best pass-catching back but he's someone Kubiak wants to design touches for in the pass game. He's the RB5 in receptions per game (4.8) and some of them are further down the field. It's a big boost to his fantasy value.

That said, Jeanty's rushing numbers and overall efficiency have been middling. He's turned RB3 overall usage into RB10 production, and his -4.4 fantasy points over expectation are the worst in the league per my model. He's below average in missed tackles forced and explosives, too. It's partially an OL issue, but the fear is that he doesn't have enough start-stop and burst to be one of the best backs in the game. This is as much of a role change that he can afford to remain a weekly top-10 back in rankings. His snaps: 74%, 81%, 84% --> 67%.

The Patriots are a tough matchup for the traveling Raiders. When healthy, they have a CB1 to cover Brock Bowers and star DTs to help stuff the run. Since last year, New England is the seventh-best fantasy RB defense when adjusting for schedule. RBs average -0.7 half PPR points versus their average. They held James Cook III to an RB16 finish last week and all RBs against them this year have been below 90 total yards. The Raiders have a 21.0-point team total (20th).

18. Bhayshul Tuten (vs. PHI) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Tuten has been a broken-tackle machine, and it's translated to RB2 value, even if he's not getting a ton of high-value touches. He's the RB33 in receptions per game (1.8), and thumping RB2 Chris Rodriguez Jr. is mixing in for scores while a segmented pass-protector RB3 steals late downs. The good news is the Jaguars are excellent, and HC Liam Coen is an RB whisperer, so high-end efficiency is part of the value. Tuten is the RB16 on RB25 usage this year.

The Eagles defense is extremely banged up. Star DT Jalen Carter (wrist) isn't himself, and LB Zack Baun (concussion), SCB Cooper DeJean (knee), CB1 Quinyon Mitchell (knee), EDGE2 Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and others are questionable to play. Philly has allowed 122 rushing YPG (10th most) this season, including a monster all-around game from Kyren Williams just last week. It's still a mediocre matchup, but it's not one to hide from like it was in the past. Jacksonville has a 24.75-point team total (sixth).

19. Jeremiyah Love (vs. DET) - 63.5 proj. total yards

Update: Love was a full participant on Friday's practice, despite having a new right ankle injury in last week's 4th quarter. If he's healthy, Love should play more than he did last week, but only he and the Cardinals know just how mobile he is. The full practice is carrying a lot of weight here. So is the awesome game environment.

20. Rhamondre Stevenson

21. David Montgomery (at TEN) - 49.5 proj. total yards

Montgomery had a couple of nice runs in Week 1, but he's been a total bust since then and is one of the least productive RBs on a per-touch basis behind a laughably bad OL. Montgomery's snap lead is also closing with Woody Marks playing the second drive of the game for the first time last week. It used to be Montgomery for the first two drives, then a drive-by-drive rotation. Montgomery is the RB23 on RB31 usage if we smooth out things across the season but I don't see the explosives or usage rebounding towards fantasy RB2 value. That said, having Nico Collins back in the mix lifts the offense's red-zone and burn-out-the-clock in the fourth quarter opportunities.

Houston has a 22.5-point team total (15th) against the 0-4 Titans as 7.5-point favorites. There are DL/OL mismatches to worry about, but the game script and projected points are in a clean spot for Montgomery to have a relative rebound this week. Of course, we all made that argument last week against the Cowboys, who held Montgomery to 24 scoreless yards on 10 carries.

22. Omarion Hampton (vs. DEN) - 37.5 proj. total yards

It's a total mess for Hampton. He's only the RB22 on RB24 usage this season, with the Chargers officially bottoming out. They potentially won't have LT Rashawn Slater (IR), RT Joe Alt and WR Ladd McConkey. Remember, it can always get worse.

The Chargers are also increasing Keaton Mitchell's and Kimani Vidal's involvement at Hampton's expense. Hampton is the RB49 in receptions per game (1.0) because he's not trusted in protection, nor is he the smoothest in the flats. What he can still do is soak up most of the goal-line scores. He did that last week to save his fantasy day (RB23 on RB29 usage).

All that said, the Broncos are missing a lot of key players (CB1 Patrick Surtain II, CB2 Riley Moss, EDGE2 Jonathan Cooper and offseason exits at DT), and they have been exposed at LB this season. Denver has allowed 143 rushing YPG (fourth most) and all four starting RBs to finish as top-20 fantasy backs. Hampton could sneak in a fine-enough outing here, but the Chargers are projected for just 19.5 points (25th).

23. RJ Harvey (at LAC) - 49.5 proj. total yards

J.K. Dobbins started, but Harvey and Tyler Badie combined for the first four carries in Week 4. Harvey played more early-down snaps than Dobbins, while Badie led the team in late-down snaps as the best protecting option. We didn't get updated goal-line usage, but it's possible Harvey is going to get more looks down there with Dobbins struggling. In the meantime, Harvey's pass-catching usage is enough for RB3 value, especially in PPR. He's the RB1 overall with 6.7 receptions per game, including his bonkers 10-grab game last week. Bo Nix's quick checkdown offense is helping Harvey, even if it's hurting the team. Harvey is the RB28 on RB33 usage this year.

24. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (vs. NYG) - 67.5 proj. total yards

The Commanders used four RBs in Week 4 without Rachaad White. Austin Ekeler split early-down snaps with Bill, while Kaytron Allen and Craig Reynolds also sprinkled in. It's all over the place in this backfield because Croskey-Merritt hasn't fully separated from the back on tape. I thought Ekeler looked better than expected!

Bill is the RB36 on RB30 usage this season and busted as the RB42 on RB27 usage last week. Bill has to score TDs to pay off because he's averaging just 1.3 receptions per game. To be fair, JCM did play more late downs last week than normal without White. But that only helps on the margins.

The Commanders project for 23.5 points with Jayden Daniels (elbow) due back. They are back at home after traveling back from London against the Giants, who won't have EDGE Brian Burns (ACL), of course. They allowed a long score from Tyler Allgeier last week, and starting RBs cleared 72 total yards in three straight games before that. It's a nice matchup in general.

25. Bucky Irving (at DAL) - 68.5 proj. total yards

Irving took a big hit to his fantasy value last week. His 8.5 expected half PPR points (RB33) were his fewest since 2024 Week 14. The Bucs offense is a total mess on tape, even across the OL, and Irving watched Sean Tucker and Kenny Gainwell score red-zone touchdowns. Tucker played three snaps, and all three of them were with one yard to go, with Irving on the field for the previous plays. Tucker is far bigger than Irving and stole Irving's goal-line TDs last year, so it's something to take seriously.

Gainwell also played the 2-minute drill and will mix in more in pure catch-up mode. Irving has played 81% of the first-quarter snaps compared to 55% of the fourth-quarter snaps this year with the Bucs sitting at 0-4. Irving still had 16 carries last week and will be in the mix for receptions (3.3 per game), but the margins are real tight. He's the RB25 on RB22 usage through the quarter mark with 6.8- and 6.1-point outings in half PPR, respectively, most recently.

The Bucs are projected for 19.5 points (26th) with an undrafted free agent QB making his second start ever on a short week on the road. The Cowboys' run defense is supposedly their strength with headliners at DT, though we haven't seen that aside from shutting down the inept Texans run game.

26. TreVeyon Henderson (vs. LV)

Update: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play.

The splits with and without Rhamondre Stevenson (knee/ankle) are staggering. Hendo has 7.1, 5.2 and 9.5 expected half PPR points this season, as the RB35 on RB44 usage. In 21 games with Rhamondre Stevenson healthy dating back to last year, Hendo is the RB44 on RB49 usage. But in three games without him, Henderson is the RB1 overall (22.7 half PPR points) on RB5 overall usage (16.5). The only backup is unproven Corey Kiner, and the Patriots don't have receiving depth right now with Mack Hollins also injured now. If Stevenson misses after not practicing on Wednesday, it's really time to party.

The Patriots project for 24.5 points as home favorites to the Raiders. Speed backs like Kenneth Walker III (179 yards), Travis Etienne Jr. (70 yards) and Omarion Hampton (115) have had success against Vegas.

26. Alvin Kamara (vs. MIN)

In his first game without Travis Etienne, Kamara had a season-high 13.9 expected half PPR points (RB18) on just seven carries while staying in the same three-back committee. Kamara converted a couple of goal-line carries and had five receptions while chasing points. He's not playing on late downs still, and Kendre Miller, who had a first-quarter fumble, is playing about a third of the early-down snaps at Kamara's expense. It's a fine role, not a bankable one.

The Saints' wild play volume is bankable at least. Kamara should have 3+ receptions based on Tyler Shough's league-leading dropbacks per game as a FLEX option, but it's hard to trust this run game without LT Kelvin Banks (ankle, IR). The Saints' RB room is averaging 26.3 expected half PPR points (eighth) and Kamara is live for at least half of them for the short term.

This week's matchup is a real test. The Vikings are second-best against fantasy RBs after adjusting for schedule, and opposing RBs are rushing less and receiving less than normal against them. The Saints are only projected for 20.5 points (22nd) this week.

29. Ollie Gordon II (vs. CIN) - 65.5 proj. total yards

The Dolphins started Jaylen Wright and gave him a couple of carries off the top, but Gordon played 60% of the snaps after that first drive, including starting the second half. Gordon finished with 7.6 expected half PPR points (RB36) on nine carries and two receptions. He made the most of his opportunities with two largely untouched runs to the left side for explosives, including one score. I can't say Gordon did anything overly impressive on tape even if the box score shows 100 rushing yards, so don't be surprised if this backfield is still up for grabs.

The Dolphins project for 18.0 points (28th) despite being at home against an inconsistent Bengals defense. Cincy has been more stout against the run (25th most YPG) with DT Dexter Lawrence than the pass (seventh most YPG), and game script should mean the Dolphins are fairly limited with their available carries here. I think Gordon's 65.5 total yards projection in the betting markets is way off base and have taken the under myself.

29. Tony Pollard (vs. HOU) - 57.5 proj. total yards

I was distracted by RT JC Latham playing like a total dawg when watching the forgettable Pollard film. The Titans OL is a bit better than expected, yet the QB play has been questionable enough to limit Pollard to RB31 half PPR points per game on RB14 usage. Last week's 21.8 expected points were a clear season high, thanks to four total goal-line opportunities. Tyjae Spears has barely run the ball but is subbing in for some obvious passing situations. Pollard is a floorless FLEX option with only 2.0 receptions per game (RB29) and a guaranteed bottom-end team total.

The Texans aren't quite the same right now with some struggling LB and DT play, but they are still only allowing 84 rush YPG (fourth best) despite facing James Cook III, Chase Brown, Jonathan Taylor and Javonte Williams. The first three finished outside the top-20 before Williams found the end zone three times last week … after CeeDee Lamb brought them to the red zone. There's nothing else to say but this matchup stinks out loud. Tennessee has a 15.5-point team total. In 12 games with the Titans scoring under 20 points, Pollard is averaging 7.6 half PPR points with a high of 12.0.

30. Will Shipley (at JAX)

Update: The Eagles got a great return (2028 second) by trading away struggling LG Cam Jurgens on Wednesday. Philadelphia has very inexperienced players at LG, C and RT right now without OL coach Jeff Stoutland there. It'll be messy, just as it was with Jurgens playing out of position coming off back surgery.

Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (hernia, IR) are out, leaving Shipley competing with practice squaders Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and Jayden Blue. Shipley has been around since 2024 as a fourth-rounder who handled huge workloads at Clemson. It'd be a total shock if he didn't comfortably lead the backfield in carries and pass-game snaps in the short term. He was already mixing in with both backs healthy in front of him.

The problem is the Eagles are next to the Browns, Dolphins and Titans on my Week 5 charts. Philly has a 17.75-point team total (29th), and they have an NFL-high 3-and-out rate in a largely broken offense. They're leading the NFL in unblocked pressure rate with a new OC, moving parts across the OL and a QB who hasn't set protections at any point in his career. It's a bad OL right now, so we're playing with fire against a loaded Jaguars DL. Jacksonville is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game (74.3) right now. Shipley is a trap with only the most desperate willing to take on the risk.

31. Mike Washington Jr. (at NE) - 16.5 proj. total yards

Update: Ashton Jeanty (toe) is a true game-time decision and the Raiders called up a practice squad RB on Saturday. This assumes Washigton plays more with Jeanty injured, but if Jeanty is out, then Washington becomes a must-start RB. He'd be my RB16, if not higher.

32. MarShawn Lloyd (vs. CHI)

Update: Chris Brooks went to injured reserve, and Kaleb Johnson was the latest to fumble. Neither option is strong for the Packers, but RBs get the rock regardless.

33. Tyler Allgeier (vs. DET) - 44.5 proj. total yards

Update: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) had a full practice on Friday.

Allgeier had a 22-yard stiff-arm touchdown and is playing in the 2-minute drills as a clear change-of-pace rusher behind Jeremiyah Love. He's hovered between 4.0 and 8.1 expected half PPR points in his last three games, but it looked like Love picked up a new ankle injury to his "other ankle" early in the fourth quarter. It's possible Allgeier is set up for a bigger workload in an amazing matchup here. Make sure he's rostered right now.

34. Brian Robinson Jr. (vs. BAL) - 35.5 proj. total yards

Shoutout to our friends with the 1.01 pick who selected Brian Robinson Jr. by accident. There have been far worse picks in the first couple rounds!!!

The Falcons are using "B-Rob" before garbage time. He's getting multiple runs in a row in the first half of games to spell Bijan, and that obviously can include goal-line work if he was out there for the previous plays. It's been enough to be the RB19 on RB40 usage this month. He's had 5.9 and 12.7 expected points in these Michael Penix Jr. starts, making him similar to Blake Corum or Chris Rodriguez Jr. as a deep-league RB3 option. He should be nearly 100% rostered as one of the most obvious insurance plans.

35. Keaton Mitchell (vs. DEN) - 30.5 proj. total yards

Mitchell's value is climbing. He's gone from 3.5 expected half PPR points in Week 2 up to 9.8 and 11.0 in the most recent games, respectively. The Chargers are losing some faith in Omarion Hampton, and Mitchell's pass-game role becomes more valuable as the defense and Ladd McConkey's foot disintegrate. Mitchell caught five passes last week and is the RB26 in receptions per game (2.3) throughout the year. He had a goal-line sweep TD this year as a bonus, but the Chargers are going to really struggle moving the ball if LT Rashawn Slater (IR) and RT Joe Alt can't play.

The Broncos are weakest at LB, however, and they are going to be missing both of their starting outside CBs. If there's a time to catch Denver slipping on defense, it's right now. These are two injured units facing off, and Mitchell is in the OC Mike McDaniel trust tree, for whatever that is worth. Kyren Williams was spammed targets in Week 3 and RB rooms against Denver are seeing 1.2 more targets than their season average, if the Chargers are still paying attention. It's hard to tell. Los Angeles has a lowly 19.5-point team total (25th).

36. Woody Marks (at TEN)

37. J.K. Dobbins (at LAC) - 61.5 proj. total yards

Dobbins played fewer early-down snaps than RJ Harvey last week, and he's averaging 0.8 receptions per game with Tyler Badie soaking up the most late-down snaps. He can't be started until proven otherwise, and there's not a real ceiling to chase on our fantasy benches. If you want to be aggressive for a pure insurance option like Kaelon Black or Tyler Allgeier, then I totally understand dropping Dobbins in shallower leagues. Dobbins is the RB48 on RB36 usage even without Jonah Coleman (IR) around.

38. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (vs. PHI) - 26.5 proj. total yards

39. Blake Corum (vs. BUF) - 31.5 proj. total yards

40. Kaleb Johnson (vs. CHI)

41. Kendre Miller (vs. MIN)

42. George Holani (vs. SF) - 35.5 proj. total yards

43. Jaylen Wright (vs. CIN) - 14.5 proj. total yards

item.title: Fight leads to two ejections at start of Jaguars vs. Eagles game in London
item.description: A fight between Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. and Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. broke out on the first play of the game. Take a look.
item.content:encoded:
The first NFL game in London this season started with fireworks – or whatever the British version of those are.

A fight broke out following the opening kickoff between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles, and the Jags' touchdown return was nullified by offsetting penalties.

Jaguars wideout Josh Cameron zoomed 90 yards to the end zone after catching the opening kickoff, but penalty flags had already been thrown by the time he reached the goal line. Holding on the Jaguars and an illegal formation by the Eagles meant their would be a re-kick.

Bryan Thomas Jr., Jeremiah Trotter Jr. ejected

Then a fight between Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. and Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. broke out near midfield. Multiple officials lost their hats, having thrown their flag already in the scrum. Five penalty flags were thrown in total. Both Thomas (a different player than Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.) and Trotter were ejected and sent to the locker room.

Replays showed that, as Cameron dashed toward the end zone, Trotter and Thomas Jr. remained entangled and their battle traversed 15 yards, into the NFL logo near midfield. Trotter shoved Thomas Jr. into the ground as Thomas Jr. appeared to try and kick Trotter from that face-up position.

Watch Eagles, Jaguars fight in London

Jeremiah Trotter and Bryan Thomas Jr. were both ejected after a scuffle during the kickoff between Eagles-Jaguars in London. pic.twitter.com/bhwh0mhKmt

— Zero Gravity (@zgsportsmedia) October 11, 2026

"So with all that going on, we just starting this whole thing over?" NFL Network broadcaster Kurt Warner joked once the ordeal ended.

The Eagles entered 2-2 while the Jaguars lead the AFC South at 3-1.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Fight leads to two ejections at start of Jaguars vs. Eagles game in London

item.title: Eagles' Jeremiah Trotter, Jaguars' Bryan Thomas ejected on opening kickoff
item.description: A crazy start in London saw a kickoff return touchdown called back on a holding penalty.
item.content:encoded:
Today's game in London had the craziest beginning of any NFL game this season.

The opening kickoff was returned for a touchdown by Jacksonville's Josh Cameron, but it was called back by a holding penalty. But that wasn't even the crazy part.

During the chaos as the officials started to call everyone back to re-do the kickoff, Philadelphia's Jeremiah Trotter and Jacksonville's Bryan Thomas fought in the middle of the field, and both were ejected, before an official play had even been run.

It's a loud and mostly pro-Eagles crowd in London, and fans who got to their seats late missed something wild.

item.title: Eagles vs. Jaguars: Live score updates, highlights, injury news
item.description: Follow along with Week 5 game updates here!
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles are in London to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 9:30 AM Eastern kickoff.

Entering this game at 2-2, the Birds are looking to avoid dropping below .500 for the first time since the 2021 NFL season. It’ll take a big effort to pull off the upset; Nick Sirianni’s squad is 7.5-point underdogs against this Jags team that’s played well since the Liam Coen era began last year.

Follow along here for live score updates, highlights, injury news, analysis, and more before this article ultimately turns into our game recap. The best place to actually discuss the game as it happens is still in our open game thread, which you can find here.

FIRST QUARTER UPDATES

  • The Eagles won the opening coin toss and decided to defer, per usual. The Jaguars took Jake Elliott’s kickoff to the house. Lol. There were flags on field after Jeremiah Trotter Jr. got in a brawl with Bryan Thomas Jr. and both players were ejected. The touchdown was also wiped out by offsetting penalties on the Eagles and Jags. Elliott kicked off again and the Jags took over at their own 26-yard line. Trevor Lawrence threw over the middle (which the Jags love to do) for a first down. Jalen Carter drew a holding penalty to knock the Jags’ offense back. Then Carter cooked the Jags’ right guard and strip-sacked Lawrence for a Jags recovery. Then a Jags false start knocked the Jags back to 2nd-and-40. What a wacky start to this game. Facing 3rd-and-37, the Jags went with a quick pass to set up a punt. Five plays, negative eight yards. Strong start by Vic Fangio’s defense.
  • The Eagles took over at their own 42-yard line after an 18-yard Britain Covey punt return. Will Shipley got the first carry of the game. Then a Jalen Hurts pass to Dallas Goedert brought up third down. Facing 3rd-and-3, Hurts hit Goedert short again for a first down. OMG! A THIRD DOWN CONVERSION! IT’S A MIRACLE! Facing 3rd-and-3 again, Hurts ran out of bounds just short of the marker. Facing 4th-and-1 from the Jags’ 37-yard line, Nick Sirianni correctly kept his offense on the field … and did NOT go tush push … but went with a shotgun handoff to Shipley, who appeared to get enough for a first down … but virtual measurement marked him short for a turnover on downs. I get it’s a backup offensive line and the tush push hasn’t been as automatic as it used to be … but that felt like a good spot for it there. At least a better option than a shotgun run. Well, at least the Eagles were able to move the ball a little bit? Six plays, 21 yards.
  • The Jags took over at their own 37-yard line. After two plays, Lawrence hit Parker Washington on a play-action boot for a 51-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Andrew Mukuba was trailing in coverage and missed the open field tackle. Looked wayyyyyy too easy for Washington to score there. EAGLES 0, JAGUARS 7.
  • The Eagles took over at their own 49-yard line after a nice 42-yard return by Britain Covey, who got lit up at the end. Hurts completed a pass to Makai Lemon, who made an impressive contested grab on a bad ball due to unblocked pressure in Hurts’ face on a boot, for no gain. Hurts’ next pass to Goedert was incomplete. Then Hurts’ third down throw to Zach Ertz along the right sideline was too high and out of bounds. Even if the pass is better, we’re really going with a go ball to a 35-year-old Ertz on 3rd-and-12? Three plays, zero yards. Terrible drive.
  • The Jags took over at their own 9-yard line and quickly picked up a first down. Facing 3rd-and-10 after a false start, Lawrence’s third down pass was short of the sticks with Quinyon Mitchell having good coverage on a curl route. Five-and-out for the Jags. Covey was hit late of out bounds but no flag on the Jags.
  • The Eagles took over at their own 36-yard line. Hurts hit Makai Lemon over the middle for a nice first down reception. Good route by the rookie to get open, good throw by Hurts into a tight window. Dameon Pierce took the first carry of his Eagles career for six yards to end the first quarter.

SECOND QUARTER UPDATES

  • The Eagles moved into field goal range but then the offense got knocked back with a Josh Hines-Allen TFL on Pierce. Facing 3rd-and-8, Nick Sirianni called a timeout with the defense seemingly showing a look the offense wasn’t ready for. Facing 3rd-and-8 for real, the Jags brought a blitz but Hurts hit Wicks on the hot read for a quick first down. Wow, you’re allowed to do that against extra pressure? Facing 3rd-and-10, Hurts hit Wicks on a slant over the middle for a first down. Nice throw for a key conversion. The Eagles went back to the spinner look but the handoff to Pierce was botched for a loss. Facing 3rd-and-goal from the 17-yard line, Hurts went to Wicks and the receiver drew a pass interference penalty on Travis Hunter. Big flag. Two plays later, Shipley found the end zone on a run up the middle, behind Willie Lampkin creating a lane. 13 plays, 64 yards, touchdown. Nice drive by the offense. EAGLES 7, JAGUARS 7.
  • The Jags took over at their own 35-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-21 after the Jags recovered Jalen Carter’s second strip-sack of the game, Lawrence’s third down pass was overthrown and incomplete. 4 plays, -11 yards, punt. Another good effort by Fangio’s defense.
  • The Eagles took over at their own 38-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-10, Hurts aired it out to Darius Cooper (the official Eagles wide receiver of Bleeding Green Nation), who made an over-the-shoulder grab and ran to the end zone for a 62-yard touchdown! EAGLES 14, JAGUARS 7.
  • The Jags took over at their own 25-yard line. The Jags instantly picked up a first down but then Carter burst through the line for a TFL. Facing 3rd-and-7, Lawrence completed a pass for a first down. Carter and Cooper DeJean then combined for another TFL. Facing 3rd-and-4 after Jalyx Hunt knocked down a Lawrence pass at the line of scrimmage, Lawrence stepped up against pressure and took off running but Hunt was able to tackle the QB short of the marker. Good pressure and really nice tackle by Hunt. Facing 4th-and-2, Liam Coen kept his offense on the field … and Michael Carter II was in position to tackle Bhayshul Tuten but the running back broke through contact to power beyond the marker. Facing 3rd-and-2, the Jags converted with a completion to the 1-yard line and called a timeout. The Jags tried to punch it in with a run but the Eagles stopped it short and the Jags took their final timeout. It looked like the Jags may have fumbled but there was no initial ruling. After replay, the ball looked to be moving before the ball carrier’s helmet touched the ground to be down by contact. Nick Sirianni called a timeout to allow more time for a review. The offense came onto the field since it looked like an Eagles recovery … but then the referees ruled the ruling on the field was upheld. OK, then. Facing 3rd-and-goal, the Jags threw incomplete with Quinyon Mitchell in good coverage on Brian Thomas Jr. and no time was left on the clock. But the refs put one second back on. Facing 4th-and-goal, the Jags went for it instead of kicking a field goal and Zack Baun was not fooled by the Jags’ sweep and instead blew up the play for a loss! 17 plays, 68 yards, zero points. Massive stop. Ball don’t lie.

The Indianapolis Colts (2-2) travel to another notorious franchise ‘House of Horrors’ to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2)(-2.5), at 1 PM EST, with expected rainy weather conditions at Acrisure Stadium for Sunday afternoon.

Rather shockingly, the Colts have not beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh since November 9, 2008, when Peyton Manning was the starting quarterback, and Indianapolis narrowly won 24-20 that Sunday afternoon.

For those looking to watch the game, it will be aired on CBS with Jim Nantz (play-by-play) and JJ Watt (analyst) covering for the television broadcast. It can also streamed on NFL+ and YouTubeTV, etc.

The NFL TV map can be found here.

Regarding those tuning in, the game can be listened to on 93.5 and 107.5 The Fan and 97.1 Hank FM, with Matt Taylor (play-by-play), Charles Arbuckle (analyst), and Larra Overton (sideline) on the radio call per usual.

For SiriusXM subscribers, you can find the Colts game on Channel 267 or 813.

Indianapolis is coming off a 2-game winning streak and currently ranks 13th in points scored (25.5 avg. ppg.), while surrendering the league’s 22nd most points (26.0 avg. ppg.). Meanwhile, Pittsburgh is 24th in points scored (19.3 avg. ppg) behind longtime veteran starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and is allowing the NFL’s 14th most points (21.8 avg. ppg.) with veterans Cam Heyward and TJ Watt still anchoring their defensive line.

There will be no former Colts wideout Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) “revenge game,” as he was recently played on injured reserve by the Steelers and is not healthy enough to face his old Indianapolis teammates.

Temperatures at kickoff are expected to be in the mid-to-high sixties, with persistent rain, potential thunderstorms, and projected wind gusts in the low teens reaching to the high twenties in miles per hour, due to lingering weather bands from Hurricane Isaias over the past week.

This week’s officiating unit will be head official Shawn Smith and his crew.

Pittsburgh has largely dominated this series all-time, holding the distinct advantage 28-8-0, and Pittsburgh earned the victory the last time these two teams played, winning 27-20 at Pittsburgh last year, on November 2, 2025.

item.title: 49ers’ unheralded D-Line is buying them a valuable luxury
item.description: The 49ers are getting healthier on a defensive line that has held up well without key players.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers will get a boost on the defensive line in Week 5, with last year’s first-round pick Mykel Williams primed to make his return against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

Williams’ first appearance since tearing his ACL last November in a win over the New York Giants will give the 49ers much-needed extra depth up front and a starter who operate as a base end and kick inside on pass-rushing downs.

And, with star edge rusher Nick Bosa seen practicing on a side field on Thursday as he targets a return in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders, the 49ers’ situation on the D-Line is looking up.

When Bosa joined Williams on the sideline with a calf injury, the Niners appeared to be in something of a desperate position on the defensive side of the trenches with C.J. West, Alfred Collins (out for the season) and Sam Okuayinonu all on injured reserve.

The injury issues the 49ers have dealt with on the defensive line furthered the perception of it being a position group in need of reinforcements via the trade market.

But the 49ers have pieced things together extremely well without a host of players expected to be D-Line contributors, with several unheralded players stepping up in hugely impressive fashion to aid both the pass rush and the run defense.

Height leads surprising pass rush performance

After missing the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals due to surgery on a broken hand, rookie edge rusher Romello Height returned in the Week 4 victory over the Denver Broncos with a club on that hand and produced the best performance of his young career.

Indeed, Height had the sixth-highest pressure rate among all edge rushers with at least 20 pass rush snaps last week, his performance with the club drawing praise from defensive coordinator Raheem Morris.

Morris told his press conference on Thursday:

“He had a couple of really good rushes. Was able to get around there and do some really good things. Obviously it’s hard to get on and off blocks sometimes. He got caught up with that [Denver Broncos OL Quinn Meinerz] 77 for that Denver team, that’s a pretty tough guy, a couple of times in there and got him in a vulnerable position. But, Romello’s a dog and I love the way he competes, the way he plays. He’s going to go out there regardless. He might have two clubs on and go out there. He’s that kind of guy. So, I’m just fired up he was able to compete and go out there and help us get a win.”

In addition to the impressive showing of Height, the 49ers got some value edge rush production from Ogbo Okoronkwo as he registered two pressures against the Broncos, per Pro Football Focus. Okoronkwo was released by the 49ers this week to make room on the 53-man roster for Williams before being re-signed to the practice squad.

Osa Odighizuwa and Keion White also stood out. Defensive tackle Odighizuwa had two pressures, with White — whose ability to operate effectively inside and out has proven a huge plus for San Francisco to start the season — had three.

Though there were expectations around Odighizuwa following his offseason trade from the Dallas Cowboys, without Bosa on the field for the last two weeks the 49ers have largely had to lean on unheralded defensive linemen for pass rush production, and the success of those lesser-known players is reflected by the fact the 49ers ended Week 4 tied fourth in the NFL with a team ESPN pass rush win rate of 56 percent.

The primary individual contributors to that number are Height, who finished Week 4 tied-sixth among all edges with 29%, and Odighizuwa, who was seventh among all defensive tackles with a win rate of 22%. However, the efforts up front have also been supplemented by the aggressiveness with which Morris is willing to use his linebackers. Dre Grenenlaw led the 49ers with four pressures against the Broncos as he was continually sent as an extra rusher, while Fred Warner has rushed the passer at his highest rate since the 2020 campaign.

Where the performance on the defensive line has not been quite as strong is in run defense.

Valdez provides reason for run D optimism

The 49ers rank 27th in run stop win rate, yet two members of their defensive tackle rotation provided significant reason for optimism in that area last Sunday. Sebastian Valdez and, to a slightly lesser extent, Naquan Jones both stood out for their play in run defense as the Broncos were limited to just 82 yards on the ground.

Both Valdez and Jones showed an ability to hold ground and violently disengage from blocks that has too often been lacking from the 49er run defense in recent times, with each player making a case for regular snaps even when the 49ers get more players back at defensive tackle, with James Thompson Jr. still out through injury.

Williams should greatly improve the 49ers’ run defense with his edge-setting prowess, while Bosa will be expected to supercharge the pass rush when he returns.

Though the displays of those who have filled the void amid injuries in recent weeks have been far from spectacular, their play has helped reduce the need for panic around the situation on the D-Line.

The 49ers don’t have any stars up front outside of Bosa, but the past two games have established that they do have a solid cast rotational defensive linemen — with Odighizuwa, White and Height the standouts — who can have enough of an impact rushing the passer and defending the run to deliver a game-winning effort.

It would be unfair not to note that the outstanding play in the back seven through the first four weeks, for which Morris deserves great praise, has clearly had an impact in minimizing the deficiencies of injury-depleted front.

But at the same time Morris and defensive line coach Kris Kocurek have found ways to get the best out of their depth guys on the D-Line, and their ability to do so has bought the 49ers a valuable luxury: patience.

The 49ers don’t have to panic. They don’t have to rush to strike a trade that gives them the extra edge rusher or interior defender they may well eventually need. John Lynch and his front office can afford to wait it out a little, safe in the knowledge that Williams and Bosa are on the way back and that the less prominent guys in the D-Line group are capable of contributing to the defensive improvement that has been obvious through the first four weeks of the season.

San Francisco probably will need to do a deal for another defensive lineman at the deadline to give the group the extra bump it may require in order for the 49ers to make a deep run in the postseason.

However, the level of play they have elicited from a group that is not externally highly thought of has bought the 49ers the time to be able to make a considered decision on the type of player they need when the deadline nears. The sack numbers aren’t gaudy and the run defense still needs to improve, but the importance of what a undermanned and unheralded defensive line has done of late shouldn’t be underestimated.

item.title: Week 5 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice
item.description: Justin Boone gets those lineups in shape for Week 5 fantasy football.
item.content:encoded:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 5 rankings. 

Starts

Matthew Stafford, QB, Rams

vs. Bills

Stafford's fantasy numbers have been a mixed bag in the opening month, with two weeks as a top-10 QB and two finishes outside the top 25. Fortunately, his next matchup has the makings for one of the best prime-time shootouts of the season. 

The Rams will host the Bills on Monday Night Football, in a game tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 54.5.

Buffalo is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing passers, including a QB1 overall result to Drake Maye last week. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Drake Maye vs. Raiders – Speaking of Maye, he finally looked more like his 2025 self in Week 4. The most exciting outcome was his season-highs in carries (8) and rushing yards (54), which Mike Vrabel highlighted as a key to their victory. If Maye keeps it up, he'll return to high-end fantasy QB1 territory. 

  • Jared Goff at Cardinals – Goff might not be at home for this one, but this is a dome game with a 54.5 projected point total against an Arizona defense that's giving up the fifth-most fantasy points to QBs.

Jaylen Warren, RB, Steelers

vs. Colts

With Rico Dowdle sitting out the last couple of games due to a toe injury, Warren has made the most of his increased workload. Despite not finding the end zone in either contest, he still racked up 302 scrimmage yards and six receptions on 44 touches during those two weeks. 

Dowdle is reportedly unlikely to play on Sunday, but even if he suits up, Warren remains a strong start after showcasing his potential recently. 

The Colts are also the eighth-best matchup for fantasy RBs, which is by far his easiest opponent through the first five weeks. You can confidently start Warren once again whether Dowdle is active or not. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Bhayshul Tuten vs. Eagles (London) – Tuten was one of my recommended buys this week, since he's been so close to much bigger stat lines recently. He's RB16 on the year, topping 85 scrimmage yards in three of his four games and is coming off season-highs in usage. He also had two TDs called back due to penalties last week. He should see plenty of work with the Jags heavily favored over the banged-up Eagles. 

  • Emanuel Wilson vs. 49ers – Wilson is coming off a 120-yard, two-touchdown effort and facing a 49ers defense that's let four different backs reach double-digit fantasy points against them in four weeks. Seattle also ran all over San Francisco in its matchups last season. 

  • Braelon Allen vs. Browns – It's hard to judge the Jets offense based on their performance in Week 4, since the Bears completely controlled the game and time of possession. Even so, Allen finished with 16 touches, including all 14 of New York's rushing attempts. I like his chances against a Browns defense allowing 103.5 scrimmage yards per game to starting RBs this season. 

Jameson Williams, WR, Lions

at Cardinals

Williams was highlighted as a start last week in this space and answered the call with six receptions and 102 yards on eight targets. Is it risky to go back to the well expecting another spike week from the volatile WR3? Yes, but fantasy managers should feel good about his outlook once again. 

In addition to being projected as a high-scoring affair in the desert, Williams also gets to face a generous Cardinals defense. Arizona is the fourth-friendliest fantasy opponent for wideouts and has given up a league-leading 11 receiving TDs. 

Other WRs to start:

  • DK Metcalf vs. Colts – With Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with a foot injury, Metcalf will be asked to carry the passing game. His nine targets in Week 4 are a promising sign of things to come and resulted in a 5-115-0 stat line versus the Browns. Indy is not a matchup to be feared. 

  • Romeo Doubs vs. Raiders – With A.J. Brown and now Mack Hollins injured, Doubs has become the focal point of New England's passing attack. Over the last three weeks, he's delivered solid numbers with 96 yards, 49 yards and then his six-catch, 58-yard, two-touchdown explosion in Week 4. The nine targets in that game are what I find the most alluring. Expect Doubs to be featured against a Raiders defense that's permitted 100-yard games to wideouts in back-to-back weeks. 

Mike Gesicki, TE, Bengals

at Dolphins

We can look to the Bengals when searching for a tight end to start this week. With Chase still working to get cleared and Higgins seeming more unlikely to be ready, Gesicki is firmly in play for fantasy. 

He's been a sneaky starter most weeks in the opening month, with touchdowns in three of his four outings. Now, he's set to benefit from the receiver injuries and see increased volume against his old team, the Dolphins. 

Miami is the fifth-best matchup for fantasy tight ends, allowing George Kittle (80 yards, TD), Travis Kelce (59 yards, TD) and T.J. Hockenson (119 yards) to have big days against them over the past three weeks. 

Editor's note: Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins will reportedly play on Sunday, which bumps down Gesicki's upside, making him more of a low-end TE1 or high-end TE2.

Other TEs to start:

  • Juwan Johnson vs. Vikings – Suggesting players to start against Minnesota's defense doesn't come without risk. However, the Vikings have given up at least 50 yards to a tight end three times in four weeks and Johnson has posted at least 50 yards in every game. He also has three touchdowns on the season. 

  • Tyler Higbee vs. Bills – With Terrance Ferguson sidelined, Higbee has found the fountain of youth, with 8-62-1 and 5-67-0 stat lines in the last two games. He's worthy of consideration as a streaming option in a potentially high-scoring MNF matchup with the Bills, who are still figuring things out under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. 

Sits

Jalen Hurts, QB, Eagles

vs. Jaguars (London)

They say things can always get worse, but the Eagles are putting that to the test at the moment. 

DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, while Dallas Goedert is expected to return from injury after a two-game absence. Wideout Dontayvion Wicks also popped up on the injury report with a new hamstring injury and a limited practice on Thursday, but will play.

To make matters worse, the offensive line is in complete disarray following the sudden retirement of Lane Johnson, the trade of Cam Jurgens and a cavalcade of injuries, including Landon Dickerson, Fred Johnson and Drew Kendall. 

Now, they're traveling to London to face a Jaguars defense that's known for shutting down the run, but has also been tough on QBs this year. This is not the time to have Hurts in your lineup. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Sam Darnold vs. 49ers – San Francisco is allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks in 2026. The Niners also held Darnold in check during their three meetings last season in Week 1 (150 yards, no TDs), Week 18 (198 yards, no TDs) and the divisional round (124 yards, TD).

  • Justin Herbert vs. Broncos – Herbert has played so poorly this year (QB22, QB24, QB23, QB27) that he's not even worth starting against a Broncos defense that will be without starting corners Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss. 

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints

vs. Vikings

While it might not have looked pretty at times, Kamara came through for fantasy managers in Week 4 with seven carries for 23 yards, five catches for 35 yards and two touchdowns on Monday Night Football. 

Hopefully no one is talking themselves into Kamara being a strong fantasy option after that game. Even with Travis Etienne Jr. on IR, Kamara still only played 38% of the snaps — sharing the load with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. 

Brian Flores' defense isn't going to make life easy on him, either. Prior to Ollie Gordon II's somewhat flukey 100-yard, one-touchdown stat line on just nine carries, the Vikings had held every back they'd faced under 50 rushing yards. On paper, Minnesota is the toughest opponent for fantasy backs in 2026. Kamara will also be playing through a back injury. The 31-year-old Kamara remains a desperation TD-or-bust RB3, who may have trouble holding up to these workloads. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Omarion Hampton vs. Broncos – Hampton's usage is trending in the wrong direction after he split snaps almost evenly with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal last week. He's managed to salvage his fantasy weeks by scoring touchdowns in three of four games so far, but that won't always be the case. Follow the volume, which led to a season-low 11 touches in Week 4.

  • Tony Pollard vs. Texans – Pollard has come through with a couple usable stat lines lately, but he's still a risky RB3 with limited scoring upside. Though the Texans defense might not be as ferocious as it was in 2025, I would still be avoiding Pollard in this matchup. 

  • J.K. Dobbins at Chargers – Dobbins has been held under 50 rushing in every game this season, has a very limited role in the passing game and hasn't found the end zone. Even a revenge game narrative against the Chargers isn't enough to convince me to start him. 

Devaughn Vele, WR, Saints

vs. Vikings

Vele has been an outstanding fantasy pickup in the opening month, with at least 50 yards in three of his games and a pair of touchdowns. 

Coming off a primetime contest where many people watched him catch six passes for 54 yards and a score, fantasy managers might be getting comfortable starting him. I'd advise against it this week. 

The Vikings are a challenging defense and Vele has benefitted from some easier matchups in the first four weeks. His only tougher opponent was the Raiders (eighth-fewest fantasy points to WRs), who held him to just three catches for 39 yards. You don't have to drop Vele until Jordyn Tyson returns, just lower your expectations against more difficult opponents like Minnesota. 

Other WRs to sit

  • Eagles WRs vs. Jaguars (London) – This probably goes without saying, but you shouldn't be mining for value on the Eagles' WR depth chart right now. Dontayvion Wicks will play after he showed up with a new injury on Thursday and Makai Lemon remains a deeper stash for later in the season. You just can't trust any of Philly's wideouts in your lineup right now with all the injuries and struggles this offense is dealing with. 

  • Courtland Sutton at Chargers – Sutton has only topped 25 yards in one game this season and is fresh off a one-catch, four-yard effort against the 49ers. Even with Pat Bryant missing time due to injury, Sutton isn't someone I'm willing to put in lineups. Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims Jr. will simply see more work in Bryant's absence. 

  • Wan'Dale Robinson vs. Texans – Robinson has found the end zone in consecutive weeks, but don't get used to it. This is a receiver who hasn't scored more than four touchdowns in an NFL season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling WR4/flex. 

T.J. Hockenson, TE, Vikings

at Saints

After missing last week with an ankle injury, Justin Jefferson practiced in a limited fashion this week. That makes it seem like he's trending in the right direction to play, but he appears to be a game-time decision and the Vikings have a Week 6 bye. So, if Minnesota wants to play it safe with the star wideout, he could sit again. 

If Jefferson plays, Hockenson goes back to being a low-end TE2 who doesn't qualify as a fantasy starter. However, even if Jefferson is ruled out, fantasy managers should be cautious about chasing Hockenson's 13-catch, 119-yard stat line from last week. 

Remember when Dalton Schultz had a 12-catch, 140-yard game for the Texans when Nico Collins was sidelined? Collins remained out the next week, but Schultz drew more defensive attention and flopped with just three catches and 30 yards. Hockenson is in a similar group at the position, making him just a risky streamer.  

Other TEs to sit:

  • Dalton Schultz at Titans – Aside from that one big blowup game, Schultz has been kept to 35 yards or less in his three other appearances. That includes just two grabs for nine yards last week. 

  • Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Ravens – Don't be tempted by Pitts' 47-yard outing last week. It came on just three catches, while running a route on just 43% of the Falcons' dropbacks. He's well off the fantasy radar and should be dropped in most redraft leagues.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Giants face Commanders in Week 5 of 2026 NFL Season
item.description: The first-place Giants travel to Washington for a big game in the NFC East against the rival Commanders in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Nobody would claim that the 2026 season has gone to plan for the Giants, who lost their starting quarterback and best defensive player to season-ending injuries. However, after four games, they find themselves on top of the NFC East with a chance to improve to 4-1 against the Washington Commanders.

Here are the key storylines to watch as the Giants look to keep the momentum going…

How long is Jameis Winston's leash?

After two disappointing games following Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury, Winston's performance in the win over the Arizona Cardinals is probably best described as a mixed bag. Winston passed for 250 yards and three touchdowns but also threw two interceptions. In many ways, it was the kind of performance people have come to expect of Winston over the years.

Washington's secondary is the weakest aspect of their defense, so you can probably expect Winston to be aggressive on Sunday, even if Malik Nabers is limited and the forecast is as foul as expected. However, J.J. McCarthy is waiting for his opportunity, having been active for the first time last weekend. Head coach John Harbaugh implied that the Giants might have a package of plays designed for McCarthy that could be unveiled at some point, too, so that will be another thing to watch for.

Arvell Reese vs. Sonny Styles

Reese and Styles were teammates at Ohio State last season, and their new teams will go head-to-head on Sunday, when comparisons between the two rookie linebackers are inevitable.

Reese was selected with the fifth overall pick in April, with Styles going two picks later. At the time, many analysts questioned why the Giants didn't just select Styles if they were planning to use Reese as a full-time linebacker anyway. However, after a slow start, Reese has had excellent performances in back-to-back weeks.

Styles is also off to a great start, although Reese has been more statistically productive and currently leads the league in solo tackles. It will be fascinating to see how they compare on Sunday.

Is John Michael Schmitz going to be back at center?

Since the Giants drafted Schmitz, he's never quite developed the level of consistency they were looking for. Could New York be planning to move on?

In the win over Arizona, Schmitz did not play after missing practice time due to the birth of his child. Bryan Hudson filled in for Schmitz and played well, leading some to speculate that the Giants intend to keep him in the starting role for the time being, even though Schmitz is fully available again.

It's possible that Schmitz being unavailable last week gave the Giants a convenient excuse for a benching, which may have been in the cards anyway. And the fact that Hudson performed so well certainly gives them options going forward.

Jayden Daniels is expected to return

Washington head coach Dan Quinn announced Friday that Daniels will make his return after missing the last two games with a dislocated left elbow, the second time in the past two seasons he's lost time with that injury. 

Marcus Mariota led the Commanders to an upset win over Seattle in his absence, only to then get hurt himself in last Sunday's loss to the Colts in London.

Daniels was a dynamic player as a rookie, but injuries have stymied his growth since. The Giants are preparing for him on the basis that he'll be 100 percent. If he is, they will need to be mindful of the run threat he provides. Daniels will be wearing a brace on his arm for the first time in his career, which could cause issues.

Time for Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux to step up

The Giants currently rank dead last in the NFL with only three sacks and are facing a Commanders team that has only given up five sacks all year, with only the 49ers having given up less than that. Nevertheless, New York will be determined to try and get after Daniels.

The Commanders' pass protection has held up well despite losing left tackle Laremy Tunsil in the preseason. They also lost their best guard, Sam Cosmi, to injury a few weeks ago, although he is set to return on Sunday.

With Brian Burns out, the Giants are relying on Carter and Thibodeaux to create pressure, and the depth on the edge will be further tested after Chauncey Golston was lost to a potential long-term injury last week. Thibodeaux has just one quarterback hit and a pass rush win rate of 0.0 percent, so New York clearly needs more from him. Carter has a sack and five quarterback hits through four games, so he could be close to a breakout.
